sentences.zh: 齊宗室諸王下

translations.literal: Northern Qi imperial clan, various princes, part two
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi Imperial Clan: Princes, Part Two

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十齊宗室諸王下

translations.literal: Biography 40: Northern Qi imperial clan, various princes, part two
translations.idiomatic: Biography 40: The Northern Qi Imperial Clan—Princes, Part Two

sentences.zh: 文襄諸子文宣諸子孝昭諸子武成諸子後主諸子

translations.literal: Sons of Wenxiang; sons of Wensuan; sons of Xiaozhao; sons of Wucheng; sons of the Last Ruler
translations.idiomatic: The Sons of Prince Wenxiang; the Sons of Emperor Wensuan; the Sons of Emperor Xiaozhao; the Sons of Emperor Wucheng; the Sons of the Last Ruler

sentences.zh: 文襄六男：文敬元皇后生河間王孝琬；

translations.literal: Wenxiang had six sons: Empress Yuan of Wenjing bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang had six sons. Empress Yuan of Wenjing bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian;

sentences.zh: 宋氏生河南王孝瑜；

translations.literal: the Song clan bore Prince Xiaoyu of Henan;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Song bore Prince Xiaoyu of Henan;

sentences.zh: 王氏生廣甯王孝珩；

translations.literal: the Wang clan bore Prince Xiaohang of Guangning;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang bore Prince Xiaohang of Guangning;

sentences.zh: 蘭陵王長恭不得母氏姓；

translations.literal: Prince Changgong of Lanling did not receive his mother's clan name;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changgong of Lanling was not given his mother's surname;

sentences.zh: 陳氏生安德王延宗；

translations.literal: the Chen clan bore Prince Yanzong of Ande;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen bore Prince Yanzong of Ande;

sentences.zh: 燕氏生漁陽王紹信。

translations.literal: the Yan clan bore Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yan bore Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 孝瑜容貌魁偉，精彩雄毅，謙慎寬厚，兼愛文學，讀書敏速，十行俱下，覆棋不失一道。

translations.literal: Xiaoyu's appearance was imposing and tall, his spirit fierce and resolute; he was modest, cautious, generous, and fond of literature; he read swiftly, ten lines at once, and in blindfold chess never missed a move.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyu was tall and imposing, with a bold and spirited bearing. Modest, cautious, and generous, he loved literature, read with exceptional speed—ten lines at a glance—and in blindfold chess never lost track of a single move.

sentences.zh: 初，文襄於鄴東起山池游觀，時俗眩之，孝瑜遂于第作水堂龍舟，植幡槊於舟上，數集諸弟，宴射為樂。

translations.literal: At first Wenxiang built hill pools and pleasure grounds east of Ye; the fashion dazzled people. Xiaoyu then made a water hall and dragon boat at his residence, planted banners and spears on the boat, and repeatedly gathered his younger brothers for feasting and archery as amusement.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wenxiang first built ornamental hills and pools for recreation east of Ye, the fashion swept the court. Xiaoyu followed suit, constructing a water hall and dragon boat at his mansion, fitting the vessel with banners and spears, and often gathering his brothers for feasts and archery.

sentences.zh: 武成幸其第，見而悅之，故盛興後園之玩。

translations.literal: Wucheng visited his residence, saw it, and was pleased; therefore the rear-garden diversions flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wucheng visited his mansion and took delight in what he saw, ornamental gardens and waterworks became all the rage at court.

sentences.zh: 於是貴賤慕斅，處處營造。

translations.literal: Thereupon nobles and commoners alike emulated it, constructing such things everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: High and low alike rushed to imitate him, building such displays everywhere.

sentences.zh: 武成嘗使和士開與胡後對坐握槊，孝瑜諫曰：「皇后天下之母，不可與臣下接手。

translations.literal: Wucheng once had He Shikai and Empress Hu sit facing each other playing liubo; Xiaoyu remonstrated, saying, "The empress is mother of the realm; she must not join hands with a subject."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng once had He Shikai and Empress Hu sit facing each other at liubo. Xiaoyu remonstrated: "The empress is mother of the realm. She must not play hand to hand with a subject."

sentences.zh: 」帝深納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 後又言趙郡王父死非命，不可而親。

translations.literal: Later he also said that Prince Rui of Zhao's father had died by violence and must not be drawn close.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to say that Prince Rui of Zhao's father had died by violence and that the prince ought not be kept close.

sentences.zh: 由是睿及士開皆側目。

translations.literal: Because of this, both Rui and He Shikai regarded him with sidelong eyes.
translations.idiomatic: From then on both Rui and He Shikai turned against him.

sentences.zh: 士開密告其奢僭，睿又言山東唯聞河南王，不聞有陛下。

translations.literal: He Shikai secretly reported his extravagance and presumption; Rui also said that east of the mountains one heard only of the Prince of Henan, not of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai secretly accused him of extravagance and overstepping his rank, while Rui told the emperor that east of the mountains people spoke only of the Prince of Henan and never of the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝由是忌之。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore came to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore grew to resent him.

sentences.zh: 爾硃御女名摩女，本事太后，孝瑜先與之通，後因太子婚夜，孝瑜竊與之言。

translations.literal: The Erzhu palace woman named Monü had formerly served the empress dowager; Xiaoyu had first had relations with her; later, on the night of the crown prince's wedding, Xiaoyu stole a word with her.
translations.idiomatic: A palace woman of Erzhu stock named Monü had once served the empress dowager. Xiaoyu had earlier taken her as a lover; later, on the night of the crown prince's wedding, he slipped away to speak with her in secret.

sentences.zh: 武成大怒，頓飲其酒三十七杯。

translations.literal: Wucheng was greatly enraged and made him drink thirty-seven cups of wine in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng flew into a rage and forced him to drink thirty-seven cups of wine in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 體至肥大，腰帶十圍，使婁子彥載以出，鴆之于車。

translations.literal: His body was extremely corpulent, his belt ten arm-spans round; he had Lou Ziyan carry him out and poisoned him in the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: His body was enormously fat—his belt ten arm-spans around. The emperor had Lou Ziyan carry him out and gave him poison in the carriage.

sentences.zh: 至西華門，煩熱躁悶，投水而絕。

translations.literal: When he reached the West Floriate Gate, feverish heat and agitation oppressed him; he threw himself into water and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the West Floriate Gate he was seized by feverish agony and threw himself into the water, where he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Commandant and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 子弘節嗣。

translations.literal: His son Hongjie succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongjie succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 廣甯王孝珩，文襄第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xiaohang of Guangning was Wenxiang's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaohang of Guangning was the second son of Prince Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 歷位司州牧、尚書令、司空、司徒、錄尚書、大將軍、大司馬。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Governor of Sizhou, Director of the Masters of Writing, Minister of Works, Minister over the Masses, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand General, and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Governor of Sizhou, Director of the Masters of Writing, Minister of Works, Minister over the Masses, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand General, and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 孝珩愛賞人物，學涉經史，好綴文，有技藝。

translations.literal: Xiaohang loved and appreciated people of talent, studied broadly in the classics and histories, enjoyed composing literary pieces, and had technical skills.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohang delighted in recognizing talent, was widely read in the classics and histories, enjoyed literary composition, and possessed various artistic skills.

sentences.zh: 嘗於査事壁自畫一蒼鷹，見者皆以為真。

translations.literal: Once on the wall of a case-inquiry room he painted a goshawk himself; viewers all took it for real.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on the wall of an office where he heard cases, he painted a goshawk with his own hand; everyone who saw it took it for a live bird.

sentences.zh: 又作朝士圖，亦當時之妙絕。

translations.literal: He also made a painting of court gentlemen, which was likewise the finest wonder of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He also painted a group portrait of court officials that was considered a masterpiece of the day.

sentences.zh: 後主自晉州敗，奔鄴，詔王公議於含光殿。

translations.literal: After the Last Ruler was defeated at Jinyang and fled to Ye, he ordered the princes and dukes to deliberate in the Hall of Contained Radiance.
translations.idiomatic: After the Last Ruler was defeated at Jinyang and fled to Ye, he summoned the princes and dukes to counsel in the Hall of Contained Radiance.

sentences.zh: 孝珩以大敵既深，事藉機變，宜使任城王領幽州道兵入土門，揚聲趣并州；

translations.literal: Xiaohang said that since the great enemy was already deep in the realm, affairs depended on swift adaptation: the Prince of Rencheng should lead Youzhou-route troops through Tumen Pass, proclaiming a march on Bingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohang argued that with the enemy already deep in Qi territory, the situation called for bold maneuver. The Prince of Rencheng should lead the Youzhou column through Tumen Pass, feigning a drive on Bingzhou;

sentences.zh: 獨孤永業領洛州道兵趣潼關，揚聲取長安。

translations.literal: Dugu Yongye should lead Luozhou-route troops toward Tong Pass, proclaiming an advance on Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Yongye should lead the Luozhou column toward Tong Pass, feigning an attack on Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 臣請領京畿兵出滏口，鼓行逆戰。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to lead the capital-region troops out through Fukou and advance with drums beating to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He himself would lead the capital troops out through Fukou and meet the enemy head-on.

sentences.zh: 敵聞南北有兵，自然潰散。

translations.literal: When the enemy heard that there were troops both north and south, they would naturally scatter in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Once the enemy heard of threats from north and south, they would surely break and flee.

sentences.zh: 又請出宮人寶物賞將士，帝不能用。

translations.literal: He also asked to distribute palace women's treasures to reward the officers and soldiers; the emperor could not adopt this.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that palace treasures be given out to reward the troops, but the emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲問孝珩齊亡所由，孝珩自陳國難，辭淚俱下，俯仰有節。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi asked Xiaohang the reasons for Qi's fall; Xiaohang himself explained the state's calamity, words and tears falling together, yet in his bearing up and down there was propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Zhou asked Xiaohang why Qi had fallen. Xiaohang spoke of the realm's ruin with tears streaming down his face, yet his bearing remained measured and dignified throughout.

sentences.zh: 憲為之改容，親為洗瘡傅藥，禮遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Xian changed expression on his account, personally washed his sores and applied medicine, and treated him with very great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was moved to change expression, personally washed his sores and applied medicine, and treated him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 孝珩獨歎曰：「李穆叔言齊氏二十八年，今果然矣！

translations.literal: Xiaohang sighed alone and said, "Li Mushu said the Qi house would last twenty-eight years—now it has indeed come to pass!
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohang sighed and said, "Li Mushu said the house of Qi would last twenty-eight years—and so it has proved!

sentences.zh: 自神武皇帝以外，吾諸父兄弟無一人得至四十者，命也。

translations.literal: Apart from Emperor Shenwu, not one of my uncles and brothers reached forty—such is fate."
translations.idiomatic: Apart from Emperor Shenwu, not one of my uncles or brothers lived to forty. That is fate."

sentences.zh: 嗣君無獨見之明，宰相非柱石之寄，恨不得握兵符，受廟算，展我心力耳。

translations.literal: The succeeding ruler lacked independent vision; the chief ministers were not pillars one could rely on. I only regret that I could not grasp the tally of command, receive the temple's strategy, and unfold the strength of my heart."
translations.idiomatic: The reigning lord lacked vision of his own; his ministers were no pillars of the state. I only wish I could have held the commander's tally, received the court's battle plan, and given my full strength to the realm."

sentences.zh: 」至長安，依例受開府、縣侯。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang'an, according to precedent he received the rank of Defender-in-Chief and Marquis of a county.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an he received, by precedent, the rank of Defender-in-Chief and a county marquisate.

sentences.zh: 後周武帝在雲陽宴齊君臣，自彈胡琵琶，命孝珩吹笛。

translations.literal: Later, Emperor Wu of Zhou, at Yunyang, feasted the Qi ruler and his ministers; he himself played the foreign pipa and ordered Xiaohang to play the flute.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at Yunyang, Emperor Wu of Zhou entertained the Qi ruler and his court. The emperor played the pipa himself and ordered Xiaohang to play the flute.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「亡國之音，不足聽也。

translations.literal: He declined, saying, "The music of a fallen state is not worth hearing."
translations.idiomatic: He declined: "The music of a fallen state is not fit to be heard."

sentences.zh: 」固命之，舉笛裁至口，淚下嗚咽，武帝乃止。

translations.literal: They pressed him firmly; he raised the flute only to his lips, tears fell and he sobbed, and Emperor Wu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When they pressed him again, he lifted the flute only to his lips, then broke down in tears. The emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 其年十月疾甚，啟歸葬山東，從之。

translations.literal: That year, in the tenth month, his illness was severe; he petitioned to be buried back in Shandong, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the tenth month, his illness grew grave. He petitioned to be buried in Shandong, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，還葬鄴。

translations.literal: Soon he died and was buried back at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was buried at Ye.

sentences.zh: 時孝琬得佛牙，置於第內，夜有神光。

translations.literal: At that time Xiaowan obtained a Buddha tooth and placed it within his residence; at night there was a divine light.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Xiaowan obtained a Buddha tooth relic and kept it in his mansion; at night a supernatural light shone forth.

sentences.zh: 照玄都法順請以奏，不從。

translations.literal: Fashun of the Xuandu Monastery asked to present it to the throne; this was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Fashun of the Xuandu Monastery asked permission to present it to the throne, but Xiaowan refused.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，使搜之，得填庫槊幡數百。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and had a search made; several hundred stored spears and banners were found.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he ordered a search of the premises and found several hundred spears and banners stockpiled in the storerooms.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，以為反狀。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and took this as evidence of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as proof of treason.

sentences.zh: 訊其諸姬，有陳氏者，無寵，誣對曰：「孝琬畫作陛下形哭之。

translations.literal: He questioned his various consorts; there was one of the Chen clan, without favor, who falsely answered, "Xiaowan painted Your Majesty's likeness and wept before it."
translations.idiomatic: He questioned Xiaowan's consorts. One Lady Chen, who had fallen out of favor, lied and said, "Xiaowan painted Your Majesty's likeness and wept before it."

sentences.zh: 」然實是文襄像，孝琬時時對之泣。

translations.literal: In fact it was Wenxiang's portrait; Xiaowan often wept before it.
translations.idiomatic: In truth it was a portrait of Prince Wenxiang, before which Xiaowan often wept.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，使武衛赫連輔玄倒鞭撾之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and had the Martial Guardsman Helian Fuxuan whip him with the reverse of the lash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had the martial guardsman Helian Fuxuan beat him with the reverse of the whip.

sentences.zh: 孝琬呼阿叔。

translations.literal: Xiaowan cried, "Uncle!".
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowan cried out, "Uncle!".

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「誰是爾叔？

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily, "Who is your uncle?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged: "Who is your uncle?

sentences.zh: 敢喚我作叔！

translations.literal: You dare call me uncle!"
translations.idiomatic: How dare you call me uncle!"

sentences.zh: 」孝琬曰：「神武皇帝嫡孫，文襄皇帝嫡子，魏孝靜皇帝外甥，何為不得喚作叔也？

translations.literal: Xiaowan said, "I am the legitimate grandson of Emperor Shenwu, the legitimate son of Emperor Wenxiang, and the nephew by marriage of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei—why may I not call you uncle?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowan replied, "I am the legitimate grandson of Emperor Shenwu, the legitimate son of Prince Wenxiang, and the nephew by marriage of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei. Why may I not call you uncle?"

sentences.zh: 」帝愈怒，折其兩脛而死。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier and broke both his shins, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier and broke both his legs, killing him.

sentences.zh: 瘞諸西山，帝崩後乃改葬。

translations.literal: He was buried on the western hills; only after the emperor's death was he reburied properly.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried on the western hills and given a proper reburial only after the emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 子正禮嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhengli succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengli succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 幼聰穎，能誦《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and sharp, and could recite the *Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals*.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was exceptionally bright and could recite the *Zuo Commentary* from memory.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，遷綿州卒。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, he was moved to Mianzhou and died there.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Qi he was relocated to Mianzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 蘭陵武王長恭，一名孝瓘，文襄第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Wu of Lanling, Changgong, also named Xiaogui, was Wenxiang's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu of Lanling, Changgong—also known as Xiaogui—was the fourth son of Prince Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 累遷并州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become Governor of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥入晉陽，長恭盡力擊之。

translations.literal: When the Turks entered Jinyang, Changgong struck them with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided Jinyang, Changgong fought them with all his might.

sentences.zh: 芒山之敗，長恭為中軍，率五百騎再入周軍，遂至金墉之下，被圍甚急。

translations.literal: At the defeat on Mount Mang, Changgong was in the center army; he led five hundred horsemen to enter the Zhou army a second time, reaching below the walls of Jinyong, where he was besieged very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: At the defeat on Mount Mang, Changgong commanded the center army. He led five hundred horsemen in a second charge into the Zhou lines and fought his way to the foot of the walls of Jinyong, where he was surrounded in desperate straits.

sentences.zh: 城上人弗識，長恭免胄示之面，乃下弩手救之，於是大捷。

translations.literal: The men on the walls did not recognize him; Changgong removed his helmet and showed his face, whereupon they lowered crossbowmen to rescue him, and thus there was a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders on the walls did not recognize him. Changgong removed his helmet and showed his face, and they sent crossbowmen down to rescue him. A great victory followed.

sentences.zh: 武士共歌謠之，為《蘭陵王入陣曲》是也。

translations.literal: The warriors together sang ballads of him; this is the *Prince of Lanling Enters the Battle Array*.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers sang ballads in his honor—the piece known as *Prince of Lanling Enters the Battle Array*.

sentences.zh: 曆司州牧、青瀛二州，頗受財貨。

translations.literal: He successively served as Governor of Sizhou and of Qing and Ying provinces, and accepted goods and wealth in considerable measure.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Sizhou and of Qing and Ying provinces, and accepted considerable bribes.

sentences.zh: 後為太尉。

translations.literal: Later he became Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 與段韶討柏穀，又攻定陽。

translations.literal: Together with Duan Shao he campaigned against Bogu and also attacked Dingyang.
translations.idiomatic: With Duan Shao he campaigned against Bogu and also attacked Dingyang.

sentences.zh: 韶病，長恭總其眾。

translations.literal: Shao fell ill, and Changgong took overall command of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao fell ill, Changgong took command of his army.

sentences.zh: 前後以戰功，別封钜鹿、長樂、樂平、高陽等郡公。

translations.literal: Before and after, for military merit he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Julu, Changlo, Leping, Gaoyang, and other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated victories he received separate enfeoffments as Duke of Julu, Changlo, Leping, Gaoyang, and other commanderies.

sentences.zh: 芒山之捷，後主謂長恭曰：「入陣太深，失利悔無所及。

translations.literal: After the victory on Mount Mang, the Last Ruler said to Changgong, "You entered the battle array too deeply; if we had lost, regret would have availed nothing."
translations.idiomatic: After the victory on Mount Mang, the Last Ruler told Changgong, "You drove too deep into the enemy lines. Had we lost, regret would have come too late."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「家事親切，不覺遂然。

translations.literal: He replied, "It was a family matter close to the heart; without noticing, it came to that."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "It was family at stake—I acted without thinking how far I had gone."

sentences.zh: 」帝嫌其稱家事，遂忌之。

translations.literal: The emperor resented his calling it a family matter and therefore came to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense at his calling it a family matter and began to harbor suspicion against him.

sentences.zh: 及在定陽，其屬尉相願謂曰：「王既受朝寄，何得如此貪殘？

translations.literal: When he was at Dingyang, his subordinate Wei Xiangyuan said to him, "Your Highness has received the court's trust—how can you be so greedy and cruel?"
translations.idiomatic: While he was at Dingyang, his subordinate Wei Xiangyuan said to him, "Your Highness bears the court's commission—how can you be so grasping and cruel?"

sentences.zh: 」長恭未答。

translations.literal: Changgong did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Changgong made no reply.

sentences.zh: 相願曰：「豈不由芒山大捷，恐以威武見忌，欲自穢乎？

translations.literal: Xiangyuan said, "Is it not because of the great victory on Mount Mang—fearing that martial prestige would draw suspicion, you wish to defile yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyuan said, "Is it not because, after your great victory on Mount Mang, you fear the throne will resent your martial glory and so you mean to discredit yourself?"

sentences.zh: 」長恭曰：「然。

translations.literal: Changgong said, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: Changgong said, "It is so."

sentences.zh: 」相願曰：「朝廷若忌王，於此犯便當行罰，求福反以速禍。

translations.literal: Xiangyuan said, "If the court resents Your Highness, on this offense punishment should be carried out at once; seeking fortune instead hastens calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyuan said, "If the court already resents you, this very offense is grounds for punishment. You seek safety but will only bring ruin faster."

sentences.zh: 」長恭泣下，前膝請以安身之術。

translations.literal: Changgong wept, advanced on his knees, and asked for a method to preserve his person.
translations.idiomatic: Changgong wept, knelt forward, and asked how he might preserve himself.

sentences.zh: 相願曰：「王前既有勳，今復告捷，威聲大重，宜屬疾在家，勿預時事。

translations.literal: Xiangyuan said, "Your Highness already had merit before; now you report victory again—your martial renown weighs heavily. You ought to plead illness and remain at home, not taking part in current affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyuan said, "You have won glory before and victory again now. Your fame is too great. You should plead illness and stay home, taking no part in affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 」長恭然其言，未能退。

translations.literal: Changgong approved his words but could not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Changgong agreed with him but could not bring himself to retire.

sentences.zh: 及江淮寇擾，恐復為將，歎曰：「我去年面腫，今何不發？

translations.literal: When bandits troubled the Jiang-Huai region, fearing he would again be made a general, he sighed and said, "Last year my face swelled—why does it not break out now?"
translations.idiomatic: When raiders troubled the Jiang-Huai region and he feared being sent to command again, he sighed: "Last year my face swelled up—why does it not flare again now?"

sentences.zh: 」自是有疾不療。

translations.literal: From then on he had an illness and would not treat it.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he let his illness go untreated.

sentences.zh: 武平四年五月，帝使徐之範飲以毒藥。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Wuping, the emperor had Xu Zhifan make him drink poison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Wuping, the emperor had Xu Zhifan give him poison to drink.

sentences.zh: 長恭謂妃鄭氏曰：「我忠以事上，何辜於天而遭鴆也？

translations.literal: Changgong said to his consort, Lady Zheng, "I served the ruler with loyalty—what offense against Heaven is there that I should meet poison?"
translations.idiomatic: Changgong said to his consort, Lady Zheng, "I served the throne in loyalty. What sin against Heaven brought me to poison?"

sentences.zh: 」妃曰：「何不求見天顏？

translations.literal: The consort said, "Why not seek to see the imperial countenance?"
translations.idiomatic: His consort said, "Why not beg an audience with the emperor?"

sentences.zh: 」長恭曰：「天顏何由可見！

translations.literal: Changgong said, "How could the imperial countenance be seen!"
translations.idiomatic: Changgong said, "How could I ever see his face again!"

sentences.zh: 」遂飲藥而薨。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drank the drug and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drank the poison and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 長恭貌柔心壯，音容兼美。

translations.literal: Changgong's appearance was gentle but his heart resolute; his voice and bearing were both beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Changgong had a gentle face but a resolute heart, and his voice and bearing were both striking.

sentences.zh: 為將，躬勤細事。

translations.literal: As a general he personally attended to minute matters.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander he personally attended to the smallest details.

sentences.zh: 每得甘美，雖一瓜數果必與將士共之。

translations.literal: Whenever he obtained something sweet and fine, even a single melon or a few fruits, he necessarily shared them with officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he obtained something choice to eat—even a single melon or a few fruits—he shared it with his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 初在瀛州，行參軍陽士深表列其贓，免官。

translations.literal: When he was first at Yingzhou, the Acting Army Aide Yang Shibiao memorialized listing his corruption; he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: While he was first at Yingzhou, the acting army aide Yang Shibiao memorialized listing his corruption, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 及討定陽，士深在軍，恐禍及。

translations.literal: When he campaigned against Dingyang, Shishen was in the army and feared disaster would reach him.
translations.idiomatic: When Changgong campaigned against Dingyang, Shibiao was with the army and feared retribution.

sentences.zh: 長恭聞之曰：「吾本無此意。

translations.literal: Changgong heard of it and said, "I originally had no such intention."
translations.idiomatic: Changgong heard of this and said, "I never had any such intention."

sentences.zh: 」乃求小失，杖深二十，以安之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sought a small fault, had Shen beaten twenty strokes, and thereby reassured him.
translations.idiomatic: He then found a minor fault in Shibiao, had him beaten twenty strokes, and so put his mind at ease.

sentences.zh: 嘗入朝而出，僕從盡散，唯有一人。

translations.literal: Once when he entered court and came out again, his attendants had all dispersed, leaving only one man.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he attended court and departed, his entire retinue had scattered, leaving only a single attendant.

sentences.zh: 長恭獨還，無所譴罰。

translations.literal: Changgong returned alone and imposed no punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Changgong returned alone and punished no one.

sentences.zh: 武成賞其功，命賈護為買妾二十人，唯受其一。

translations.literal: Wucheng rewarded his merit and ordered Jia Hu to buy twenty concubines for him; he accepted only one.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng rewarded his achievements and had Jia Hu purchase twenty concubines for him, but he accepted only one.

sentences.zh: 有千金責券，臨死悉燔之。

translations.literal: He had promissory notes for a thousand gold; on the verge of death he burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: He held debt notes worth a thousand gold; on his deathbed he burned them all.

sentences.zh: 安德王延宗，文襄第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Yanzong of Ande was Wenxiang's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yanzong of Ande was the fifth son of Prince Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 母陳氏，廣陽王妓也。

translations.literal: His mother was of the Chen clan, a courtesan of Prince Guangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Chen, a courtesan in the household of the Prince of Guangyang.

sentences.zh: 延宗幼為文宣所養。

translations.literal: In youth Yanzong was raised by Wensuan.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood Yanzong was raised by Emperor Wensuan.

sentences.zh: 年十二，猶騎置腹上，令溺己臍中。

translations.literal: At age twelve he was still set astride the belly and made to urinate into the navel.
translations.idiomatic: Even at twelve he was set astride the belly and made to urinate into the navel.

sentences.zh: 抱之曰：「可憐，止有此一個。

translations.literal: Holding him, he said, "Poor child—you are the only one."
translations.idiomatic: Cradling him, he said, "Poor boy—you are the only one I have."

sentences.zh: 」問欲作何王，對曰：「欲作沖天王。

translations.literal: He asked what prince he wished to become; he answered, "I wish to become Prince Sky-Storming."
translations.idiomatic: Asked what title he wanted, the boy replied, "I want to be Prince Sky-Storming."

sentences.zh: 」文宣問楊愔，愔曰：「天下無此郡名，願使安於德。

translations.literal: Wensuan asked Yang Yin; Yin said, "There is no such commandery name in the realm; may he rest in virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Wensuan consulted Yang Yin, who said, "No such commandery exists in the realm. Let him rest in virtue instead."

sentences.zh: 」於是封安德焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ande.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore enfeoffed as Prince of Ande.

sentences.zh: 為定州刺史。

translations.literal: He became Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 於樓上大便，使人在下，張口承之。

translations.literal: On the upper story he defecated, having men below open their mouths to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved himself from an upper story while men below opened their mouths to catch the filth.

sentences.zh: 以蒸豬糝和人糞以飼左右，有難色者鞭之。

translations.literal: He mixed steamed pork meal with human excrement to feed his attendants; those who showed distaste he whipped.
translations.idiomatic: He fed his attendants a mash of steamed pork meal mixed with human excrement and whipped anyone who showed disgust.

sentences.zh: 孝昭帝聞之，使趙道德就州杖之一百。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao heard of this and sent Zhao Daode to the province to beat him one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao heard of this, he sent Zhao Daode to the province to beat him one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 道德以延宗受杖不謹，又加三十。

translations.literal: Because Yanzong did not receive the beating with proper care, Daode added thirty more.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yanzong did not submit properly to the beating, Daode added thirty strokes.

sentences.zh: 又以囚試刀，驗其利鈍。

translations.literal: He also tested blades on prisoners to verify their sharpness or dullness.
translations.idiomatic: He also tested his blades on prisoners to see whether they were sharp or dull.

sentences.zh: 驕縱多不法。

translations.literal: Arrogant and unrestrained, he committed many unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant and lawless, he committed many outrages.

sentences.zh: 武成使撻之，殺其昵近九人，從是深自改悔。

translations.literal: Wucheng had him thrashed and killed nine of his intimates; from then on he deeply reformed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng had him beaten and killed nine of his close companions; from then on he deeply reformed himself.

sentences.zh: 蘭陵王芒山凱捷，自陳兵勢，諸兄弟咸壯之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lanling won victory on Mount Mang, he himself described his military strength, and all the brothers admired him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Changgong of Lanling won his victory on Mount Mang and described his military strength, all his brothers were impressed.

sentences.zh: 延宗獨曰：「四兄非大丈夫，何不乘勝徑入？

translations.literal: Yanzong alone said, "My four elder brothers are no true men—why did they not press the advantage and advance straight in?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong alone said, "My four elder brothers are no true men. Why did they not press the victory and drive straight in?"

sentences.zh: 使延宗當此勢，關西豈得復存！

translations.literal: Had Yanzong been in that position, how could the lands west of the passes still have survived!
translations.idiomatic: Had I been in their place, the lands west of the passes would not still be standing!

sentences.zh: 」及蘭陵死，妃鄭氏以頸珠施佛，廣甯王使贖之，延宗手書以諫，而淚滿紙。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lanling died, his consort Lady Zheng gave a neck pearl to the Buddha; the Prince of Guangning sent to redeem it; Yanzong wrote a letter of remonstrance by hand, and tears filled the paper.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Changgong died, his consort Lady Zheng donated a neck pearl to a Buddhist temple. Prince Xiaohang of Guangning sent to redeem it; Yanzong wrote a remonstrance in his own hand, the paper soaked with tears.

sentences.zh: 河間死，延宗哭之，淚赤。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Hejian died, Yanzong mourned him until his tears ran red.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiaowan of Hejian died, Yanzong wept until his tears ran red.

sentences.zh: 又為草人以像武成，鞭而訊之曰：「何故殺我兄！

translations.literal: He also made a straw figure in Wucheng's likeness, whipped it, and interrogated it, saying, "Why did you kill my brother!"
translations.idiomatic: He fashioned a straw effigy of Wucheng, whipped it, and demanded, "Why did you kill my brother!"

sentences.zh: 」奴告之，武成覆臥延宗于地，馬鞭撾之二百，幾死。

translations.literal: A slave reported this; Wucheng threw Yanzong face down on the ground and beat him two hundred strokes with a horsewhip, nearly killing him.
translations.idiomatic: A slave reported this. Wucheng threw Yanzong face down and beat him two hundred strokes with a horsewhip, nearly killing him.

sentences.zh: 後曆司徒、太尉。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Minister over the Masses and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Minister over the Masses and Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 及平陽之役，後主自禦之，命延宗率右軍，先戰城下，禽周開府宗挺。

translations.literal: At the campaign of Pingyang, the Last Ruler personally took command and ordered Yanzong to lead the right army; he fought first below the walls and captured Zhou Defender-in-Chief Zong Ting.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Pingyang the Last Ruler took personal command and ordered Yanzong to lead the right wing. Yanzong fought first below the walls and captured the Zhou Defender-in-Chief Zong Ting.

sentences.zh: 及大戰，延宗以麾下再入，周軍莫不披靡。

translations.literal: In the great battle, Yanzong with his subordinates entered a second time, and the Zhou army was everywhere routed.
translations.idiomatic: In the great battle Yanzong led his men in a second charge, and the Zhou army broke everywhere before him.

sentences.zh: 諸軍敗，延宗獨全軍。

translations.literal: When the armies were defeated, Yanzong alone preserved his army intact.
translations.idiomatic: When the other armies were routed, Yanzong alone brought his force out intact.

sentences.zh: 後主將奔晉陽，延宗言：「大家但在營莫動，以兵馬付臣，臣能破之。

translations.literal: When the Last Ruler was about to flee to Jinyang, Yanzong said, "Your Majesty need only remain in camp without moving and entrust the horses and troops to your servant; your servant can break them."
translations.idiomatic: As the Last Ruler prepared to flee to Jinyang, Yanzong said, "Your Majesty need only stay in camp and give me the army. I can break the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及至并州，又聞周軍已入鸑鼠穀。

translations.literal: When he reached Bingzhou, he again heard that the Zhou army had entered Quezui Valley.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Bingzhou, he learned that the Zhou army had already entered Quezui Valley.

sentences.zh: 乃以延宗為相國、并州刺史，總山西兵事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made Yanzong Chancellor of State and Governor of Bingzhou, putting him in overall charge of military affairs west of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Yanzong Chancellor of State and Governor of Bingzhou, entrusting him with all military affairs west of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「并州阿兄取，兒今去也。

translations.literal: He said to him, "Bingzhou, elder brother, is yours to take; your son now departs."
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "Bingzhou is yours, elder brother. Your son is leaving now."

sentences.zh: 」延宗曰：「陛下為社稷莫動，臣為陛下出死力戰。

translations.literal: Yanzong said, "Your Majesty, for the sake of the altars of state, do not move; your servant will go forth and fight to the death for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong said, "For the sake of the realm, Your Majesty must not flee. I will fight to the death for you."

sentences.zh: 」駱提婆曰：「至尊計已成，王不得輒沮。

translations.literal: Luo Tipo said, "The Supreme One's plan is already settled; Your Highness must not obstruct it."
translations.idiomatic: Luo Tipo said, "His Majesty's plan is already set. Your Highness must not stand in the way."

sentences.zh: 」後主竟奔鄴。

translations.literal: The Last Ruler ultimately fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Ruler fled to Ye after all.

sentences.zh: 在並將卒咸請曰：「王若不作天子，諸人實不能與王出死力。

translations.literal: At Bing, generals and soldiers all pleaded, "If Your Highness will not become Son of Heaven, we truly cannot fight to the death for you."
translations.idiomatic: The generals and soldiers at Bing all pleaded, "Unless Your Highness takes the throne, we cannot fight to the death for you."

sentences.zh: 」延宗不得已，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Yanzong, having no choice, thereupon assumed the imperial position.
translations.idiomatic: With no alternative, Yanzong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「武平孱弱，政由宦豎，釁結蕭牆，盜起疆場。

translations.literal: He issued an edict saying, "The Wuping reign was feeble; government lay in eunuchs; calamity arose within the palace walls; bandits rose on the borders."
translations.idiomatic: His edict read: "The Wuping reign was feeble, government was in the hands of eunuchs, disaster arose within the palace, and enemies rose on the frontiers."

sentences.zh: 斬關夜遁，莫知所之，則我高祖之業，將墜於地。

translations.literal: Breaking through the passes by night and fleeing, none knew where he had gone—then the enterprise of our High Ancestor would have fallen to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler fled by night through the passes, and none knew where he had gone. The enterprise of our High Ancestor would have collapsed.

sentences.zh: 王公卿士，猥見推逼，今便祗承寶位，可大赦天下。

translations.literal: The princes, dukes, and ministers, though I was unworthily pressed forward, now reverently accept the precious throne; a general amnesty is proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The princes, dukes, and ministers, though they pressed this unworthy man forward, now I reverently accept the throne. Let there be a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 」改武平七年為德昌元年，以晉昌王唐邕為宰輔，齊昌王莫多婁敬顯、沐陽王和阿於子、右衛大將軍段暢、武衛將軍相裏僧伽、開府韓骨胡、侯莫陳洛州為爪牙。

translations.literal: He changed the seventh year of Wuping to the first year of Dechang; he made Prince Jinchang Tang Yong Chancellor, Prince Qichang Moduolou Jingxian, Prince of Muyang He Aziyu, Right Guards General Duan Chang, Martial Guards General Xiangli Sengqia, Defender-in-Chief Han Guhu, and Houmochen Luozhou his strong arms.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the seventh year of Wuping to the first year of Dechang. He appointed Prince Jinchang Tang Yong as chief minister, with Prince Qichang Moduolou Jingxian, Prince of Muyang He Aziyu, Right Guards General Duan Chang, Martial Guards General Xiangli Sengqia, Defender-in-Chief Han Guhu, and Houmochen Luozhou as his chief supporters.

sentences.zh: 眾聞之，不召而至者前後相屬。

translations.literal: When the masses heard this, those who came unbidden before and after were continuous.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread, men came of their own accord in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 延宗容貌充壯，坐則仰，偃則伏，人皆笑之。

translations.literal: Yanzong's physique was full and strong; seated he leaned back, lying down he sprawled face down—people all laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong was stout and powerful, but when he sat he leaned back and when he lay down he sprawled face down, and everyone laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 及是，赫然奮發，氣力絕異，馳騁行陣，勁捷若飛。

translations.literal: Now, however, he blazed forth in spirit; his strength was utterly unlike before; galloping through the battle lines he was as nimble as flight.
translations.idiomatic: Now he blazed with energy. His strength was extraordinary, and galloping through the ranks he was swift as flight.

sentences.zh: 傾府藏及後宮美女以賜將士，籍沒內參千餘家。

translations.literal: He emptied the treasury and palace beauties to reward officers and soldiers, and confiscated the property of more than a thousand inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He emptied the treasury and distributed palace women to reward the troops, and confiscated the property of more than a thousand inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 後主謂近臣曰：「我甯使周得并州，不欲安德得之！

translations.literal: The Last Ruler said to his close attendants, "I would rather let Zhou take Bingzhou than let Ande have it!"
translations.idiomatic: The Last Ruler told his intimates, "I would rather Zhou take Bingzhou than let Ande have it!"

sentences.zh: 」左右曰：「理然。

translations.literal: His attendants said, "That is reasonable."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "That is only reasonable."

sentences.zh: 」延宗見士卒，皆親執手陳辭，自稱名，流涕嗚噎。

translations.literal: Yanzong, seeing the soldiers, personally took each man's hand and spoke to him, giving his own name, weeping and choking with sobs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong went among the soldiers, took each man's hand, spoke to him by name, and wept until he could barely speak.

sentences.zh: 眾皆爭為死，童兒女子亦乘屋攘袂，投磚石以禦周軍。

translations.literal: The masses all vied to die for him; boys and girls too climbed onto roofs, rolled up their sleeves, and cast bricks and stones against the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: All vowed to die for him. Even boys and girls climbed onto roofs, rolled up their sleeves, and hurled bricks and stones at the Zhou army.

sentences.zh: 特進、開府那盧安生守太谷，以萬兵叛。

translations.literal: Special Adviser and Defender-in-Chief Nalu Ansheng held Tai Valley with ten thousand men and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Nalu Ansheng, Special Adviser and Defender-in-Chief, held Tai Valley with ten thousand men and went over to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 周軍圍晉陽，望之如黑雲四合。

translations.literal: The Zhou army besieged Jinyang; viewed from afar it was like black clouds closing in on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army besieged Jinyang. From a distance it looked like black clouds closing in from every side.

sentences.zh: 延宗命莫多婁敬顯、韓骨胡拒城南；

translations.literal: Yanzong ordered Moduolou Jingxian and Han Guhu to hold the south of the city;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong ordered Moduolou Jingxian and Han Guhu to hold the south wall;

sentences.zh: 和阿于子、段暢拒城東；

translations.literal: He Aziyu and Duan Chang to hold the east of the city;
translations.idiomatic: He Aziyu and Duan Chang to hold the east wall;

sentences.zh: 延宗親當周齊王於城北，奮大槊往來督戰，所向無前。

translations.literal: Yanzong personally faced Prince Xian of Zhou at the north of the city, wielding a great spear back and forth to direct the battle, advancing wherever he went without opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong personally faced Prince Xian of Zhou at the north wall, wielding a great spear and directing the battle, irresistible wherever he turned.

sentences.zh: 尚書令史沮山亦肥大多力，捉長刀步從，殺傷甚多。

translations.literal: Recorder of the Masters of Writing Zu Shan was also corpulent and very strong; grasping a long blade he followed on foot, killing and wounding many.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Shan, a clerk in the Masters of Writing office, was also stout and very strong. He followed on foot with a long blade and killed or wounded many.

sentences.zh: 武衛蘭芙蓉、綦連延長皆死於陣。

translations.literal: Martial Guards Lan Furong and Qilian Yanchang both died in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: The martial guards Lan Furong and Qilian Yanchang both fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 和阿于子、段暢以千騎投周軍，周軍攻東門，際昏遂入。

translations.literal: He Aziyu and Duan Chang with a thousand horsemen went over to the Zhou army; the Zhou army attacked the east gate and at dusk entered.
translations.idiomatic: He Aziyu and Duan Chang defected to the Zhou with a thousand horsemen. The Zhou attacked the east gate and broke in at dusk.

sentences.zh: 進兵焚佛寺門屋，飛焰照天地。

translations.literal: Advancing, they burned the gate and roof-beams of the Buddhist temple; flying flames lit heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced and set fire to the Buddhist temple gate and halls; flames lit heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 延宗與敬顯自門入，夾擊之，周軍大亂，爭門相填。

translations.literal: Yanzong and Jingxian entered from the gate and struck from both sides; the Zhou army was greatly thrown into disorder, struggling at the gate and blocking one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong and Jingxian entered through the gate and attacked from both sides. The Zhou army fell into chaos, men jamming the gate and trampling one another.

sentences.zh: 齊人後斫刺，死者一千餘人。

translations.literal: The Qi men stabbed from behind; more than a thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi soldiers struck from behind, and more than a thousand perished.

sentences.zh: 周武帝左右略盡，自拔無路。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou's attendants were nearly all gone; he could find no way to pull himself free.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou's attendants were nearly all gone, and he could find no way to escape.

sentences.zh: 承禦上士張壽輒牽馬頭，賀拔佛恩以鞭拂其後，以崎嶇僅得出。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhang Shou abruptly seized the horse's head; Heba Fo'en struck its hindquarters with a whip; by rugged paths he barely got out.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zhang Shou seized the horse's head, and Heba Fo'en lashed its hindquarters. By rugged paths the emperor barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 齊人奮擊，幾中馬。

translations.literal: The Qi men pressed the attack and nearly struck the horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi pressed the attack and nearly struck the horse.

sentences.zh: 城東厄曲，佛恩及降者皮子信為之導，僅免。

translations.literal: East of the city the road was narrow and winding; Fo'en and the defector Pizi Xin guided him, and he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: East of the city the road was narrow and winding. Fo'en and the defector Pizi Xin guided him, and he barely got away.

sentences.zh: 時四更也。

translations.literal: It was then the fourth watch.
translations.idiomatic: It was the fourth watch of the night.

sentences.zh: 延宗謂周武帝崩於亂兵，使於積屍中求長鬣者，不得。

translations.literal: Yanzong thought Emperor Wu of Zhou had perished in the confused fighting and had them search the heaped corpses for a man with long whiskers, but they did not find him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong thought the Zhou emperor had died in the melee and had the corpses searched for a man with long whiskers, but found nothing.

sentences.zh: 時齊人既勝，入坊飲酒，盡醉臥，延宗不復能整。

translations.literal: At that time the Qi men, having won, entered the wards to drink wine, all drunk and asleep; Yanzong could no longer restore order.
translations.idiomatic: The victorious Qi troops went into the wards to drink, fell drunk asleep, and Yanzong could no longer restore order.

sentences.zh: 周武帝出城，饑甚，欲為遁逸計。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou left the city; he was very hungry and thought of escape.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor left the city starving and considered flight.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲及柱國王誼諫，以為去必不免。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Zhou and Pillar of State Wang Yi remonstrated, saying that if they left they would surely not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Zhou and Pillar of State Wang Yi urged that flight would mean certain capture.

sentences.zh: 延宗叛將段暢亦盛言城內空虛。

translations.literal: Yanzong's defector Duan Chang also strongly said the city inside was empty.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong's defector Duan Chang also insisted the city was empty within.

sentences.zh: 周武帝乃駐馬，鳴角收兵，俄傾復振。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou then halted his horse, sounded the horn to gather troops, and soon his forces rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor halted, sounded the horn to rally his men, and soon his army regrouped.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，還攻東門，克之。

translations.literal: At dawn he returned to attack the east gate and took it.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he attacked the east gate again and took it.

sentences.zh: 又入南門。

translations.literal: He also entered the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: He also entered through the south gate.

sentences.zh: 延宗戰，力屈，走至城北，於人家見禽。

translations.literal: Yanzong fought until his strength was spent, fled to the north of the city, and at a private house was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong fought until exhausted, fled to the north of the city, and was captured in a private house.

sentences.zh: 周武帝自投下馬，執其手。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou dismounted of his own accord and grasped his hand.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor dismounted and took his hand.

sentences.zh: 延宗辭曰：「死人手何敢迫至尊！

translations.literal: Yanzong declined, saying, "How dare a dead man's hand press upon the Supreme One!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong protested, "How dare the hand of a dead man touch Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「兩國天子，有何怨惡？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What enmity is there between two sons of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What enmity lies between two sons of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 直為百姓來耳！

translations.literal: I have come only for the sake of the common people!
translations.idiomatic: I have come only for the sake of the people!

sentences.zh: 勿怖，終不相害。

translations.literal: Do not fear—I will never harm you.
translations.idiomatic: Do not be afraid. I will never harm you.

sentences.zh: 」使復衣帽，禮之。

translations.literal: He had his hat and robes restored and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yanzong's hat and robes restored and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 先是，高都郡有山焉，絕壁臨水，忽有墨書云：「齊亡延宗。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Gaodu Commandery there was a mountain with sheer cliffs over water; suddenly there appeared writing in ink saying, "Qi falls—Yanzong."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Gaodu Commandery, a cliff overhanging the water bore writing in ink: "Qi falls—Yanzong."

sentences.zh: 」洗視，逾明。

translations.literal: When washed and viewed, it grew clearer.
translations.idiomatic: When washed, the characters grew clearer.

sentences.zh: 帝使人就寫，使者改亡為上。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a man to copy it; the envoy changed "fall" to "rise."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a man to copy it; the envoy changed "fall" to "rise."

sentences.zh: 至是應焉。

translations.literal: Now this came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Now the prophecy was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 延宗敗前，在鄴聽事，以十二月十三日晡時受敕守并州，明日建尊號。

translations.literal: Before Yanzong's defeat, at Ye in the audience hall, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month at the hour of the ram he received orders to guard Bingzhou; the next day he would establish his imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: Before his defeat, at Ye in the audience hall, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month at the hour of the ram he received orders to guard Bingzhou; the next day he was to proclaim himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 不間日而被圍，經宿，至食時而敗。

translations.literal: Within a day he was besieged; after one night, by mealtime he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Within a day he was besieged; after one night, by mealtime, he was defeated.

sentences.zh: 年號德昌。

translations.literal: His reign title was Dechang.
translations.idiomatic: His reign title was Dechang.

sentences.zh: 好事者言其得二日云。

translations.literal: Wits said he had got two days.
translations.idiomatic: Wits said he had reigned for two days.

sentences.zh: 既而周武帝問取鄴計，辭曰：「亡國大夫不可以圖存，此非臣所及。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Wu of Zhou asked his plan for taking Ye; he declined, saying, "A minister of a fallen state cannot plot survival—this is not within my competence."
translations.idiomatic: Later the Zhou emperor asked his plan for taking Ye. He declined: "A minister of a fallen state cannot plot survival. That is beyond me."

sentences.zh: 」強問之，乃曰：「若任城王援鄴，臣不能知；

translations.literal: Pressed to answer, he finally said, "If the Prince of Rencheng comes to relieve Ye, your servant cannot know;
translations.idiomatic: Pressed hard, he finally said, "If the Prince of Rencheng comes to relieve Ye, I cannot say;

sentences.zh: 若今主自守，陛下兵不血刃。

translations.literal: if the present ruler holds it himself, Your Majesty's army will take it without shedding blood.
translations.idiomatic: but if the present ruler holds it himself, Your Majesty's army will take it without shedding blood."

sentences.zh: 」及至長安，周武與齊君臣飲酒，令後主起舞。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang'an, Zhou Wu drank with the Qi ruler and his ministers and ordered the Last Ruler to dance.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an the Zhou emperor feasted with the Qi ruler and his ministers and ordered the Last Ruler to dance.

sentences.zh: 延宗悲不自持，屢欲仰藥自裁，侍婢苦執諫而止。

translations.literal: Yanzong could not contain his grief; repeatedly he wished to take poison and kill himself, but serving maids firmly held him and remonstrated until he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong was overcome with grief and several times tried to take poison, but his serving maids held him back and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，周武誣後主及延宗等，雲遙應穆提婆反，使並賜死。

translations.literal: Before long Zhou Wu falsely accused the Last Ruler, Yanzong, and others of secretly responding to Mutipo's rebellion and had them all sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Zhou emperor falsely accused the Last Ruler, Yanzong, and others of plotting with Mutipo and had them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 皆自陳無之，延宗攘袂，泣而不言。

translations.literal: All declared themselves innocent; Yanzong rolled up his sleeves, weeping but saying nothing.
translations.idiomatic: All protested their innocence. Yanzong rolled up his sleeves, weeping in silence.

sentences.zh: 以椒塞口而死。

translations.literal: They died with pepper stuffed in their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: They were killed with pepper stuffed in their mouths.

sentences.zh: 明年，李妃收殯之。

translations.literal: The next year, Lady Li gathered his remains for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Lady Li collected his body for proper burial.

sentences.zh: 後主之傳位於太子也，孫正言竊謂人曰：「我昔武定中為廣州士曹，聞襄城人曹普演有言：高王諸兒，阿保當為天子，至高德之承之，當滅。

translations.literal: When the Last Ruler abdicated in favor of the crown prince, Sun Zhengyan privately told others, "In the past, during the Wuding era, I served as a staff officer in Guangzhou and heard CaO Puyan of Xiangcheng say: Among the sons of Prince Gao, Abao would become emperor; by the time of De and Cheng, [the dynasty] would perish.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Ruler abdicated to the crown prince, Sun Zhengyan confided to others, "During the Wuding era I had served as a staff officer in Guangzhou and heard CaO Puyan of Xiangcheng prophesy: Among Prince Gao's sons, Abao would reign as emperor; when De and Cheng came in succession, the dynasty would fall.

sentences.zh: 阿保謂天保，德之謂德昌也，承之謂後主年號承元，其言竟信云。」

translations.literal: Abao meant Tianbao, De meant Dechang, and Cheng meant the Last Ruler's reign title Chengyuan—and in the end his words proved true."
translations.idiomatic: Abao referred to Tianbao, De to Dechang, and Cheng to the Last Ruler's era name Chengyuan—and in the end the prophecy came true."

sentences.zh: 漁陽王紹信，文襄第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang was Wenxiang's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang was the sixth son of Prince Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 曆特進、開府、中領軍、護軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Special Adviser, Defender-in-Chief, Director of the Central Army, Director of the Guards, and Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Special Adviser, Defender-in-Chief, Director of the Central Army, Director of the Guards, and Governor of Qing.

sentences.zh: 行過漁陽，與大富人鐘長命同床坐，太守鄭道蓋來謁，長命欲起，紹信不聽曰：「此何物小人，主人公為起！

translations.literal: Passing through Yuyang, he sat on the same couch with the great magnate Zhong Changming; when the prefect Zheng Daogai came to pay his respects, Changming wished to rise, but Shaoxin would not allow it, saying, "What sort of petty man is this, that the master of the house should rise for him!
translations.idiomatic: While passing through Yuyang he shared a couch with the wealthy Zhong Changming. When Prefect Zheng Daogai came to pay his respects, Changming started to rise, but Shaoxin stopped him, saying, "What kind of nobody is this, that the master of the house should stand for him!

sentences.zh: 」乃與長命結為義兄弟，妃與長命妻為姊妹，責其闔家長幼，皆有贈賄，鐘氏因此遂貧。

translations.literal: 」He then swore brotherhood with Changming, and his consort with Changming's wife became sworn sisters; he demanded gifts from every member of the household, young and old, and the Zhong clan was ruined by it.
translations.idiomatic: 」He then entered sworn brotherhood with Changming, and his consort with Changming's wife became sworn sisters. He exacted gifts from every member of the Zhong household, young and old, until the clan was reduced to poverty.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，死于長安。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, he died in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi fell, he died in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 文宣五男，李後生廢帝及太原王紹德；

translations.literal: Wensuan had five sons: Empress Li bore the Deposed Emperor and Prince Shaode of Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wensuan had five sons. Empress Li bore the Deposed Emperor and Prince Shaode of Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 馮世婦生范陽王紹義；

translations.literal: Lady Feng of the Shi household bore Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng bore Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang;

sentences.zh: 裴嬪生西河王紹仁；

translations.literal: Consort Pei bore Prince Shaoren of Xihe;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pei bore Prince Shaoren of Xihe;

sentences.zh: 顏嬪生隴西王紹廉。

translations.literal: Consort Yan bore Prince Shaolian of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yan bore Prince Shaolian of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 太原王紹德，文宣第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Shaode of Taiyuan was Wensuan's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaode of Taiyuan was the second son of Emperor Wensuan.

sentences.zh: 天保末，為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, he was made Defender-in-Chief with Equivalence to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he held the rank of Defender-in-Chief with Equivalence to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 武成因怒李後，罵紹德曰：「爾父打我時，竟不來救。

translations.literal: Because Wucheng was enraged at Empress Li, he reviled Shaode, saying, "When your father was beating me, you never came to my rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Angered at Empress Li, Emperor Wucheng cursed Shaode, saying, "When your father was beating me, you never came to save me.

sentences.zh: 」以刀環築殺之，親以土埋之遊豫園。

translations.literal: 」He killed him by striking with the ring of his sword and personally buried him with earth in the Garden of Roaming Pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: 」He beat him to death with the ring of his sword and personally buried him in the Garden of Roaming Pleasure.

sentences.zh: 武平元年，詔以范陽王子辨才為後，襲太原王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuping, an edict made Prince Biancai of Fanyang Shaode's heir and successor as Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping, an edict appointed Prince Biancai of Fanyang as Shaode's heir to succeed to the title Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 范陽王紹義，文宣第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang was Wensuan's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang was the third son of Emperor Wensuan.

sentences.zh: 初封廣陽，徙封范陽。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangyang, then transferred to Prince of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Guangyang, then transferred to Prince of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 歷位侍中、清都尹。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Palace Attendant and Director of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Palace Attendant and Director of the Capital District.

sentences.zh: 好與群小同飲，擅致內參打殺博士任方榮。

translations.literal: He liked to drink with petty men and on his own authority had inner attendants beat and kill Doctor Ren Fangrong.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to drink with low companions and on his own authority had palace attendants beat Doctor Ren Fangrong to death.

sentences.zh: 武成嘗杖之二百，送付昭信後，後又杖一百。

translations.literal: Wucheng once had him beaten two hundred strokes and sent him to Empress Zhaoxin; later he was beaten another hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng once had him beaten two hundred strokes and sent him to Empress Zhaoxin; later he received another hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 及後主奔鄴，以紹義為尚書令、定州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Last Ruler fled to Ye, Shaoyi was made Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Ruler fled to Ye, Shaoyi was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Ding.

sentences.zh: 周武帝克并州，以封輔相為北朔州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou took Bingzhou, he made Feng Fuxiang Commander-in-Chief of Northern Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Zhou captured Bingzhou, he appointed Feng Fuxiang Commander-in-Chief of Northern Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 此地齊之重鎮，諸勇士多聚焉。

translations.literal: This place was a vital stronghold of Qi, and many brave warriors gathered there.
translations.idiomatic: The region was a vital Qi stronghold where many fierce warriors had gathered.

sentences.zh: 前長史趙穆、司馬王當萬等謀執輔相，迎任城王於瀛州。

translations.literal: The former chief clerk Zhao Mu, the aide Wang Dangwan, and others plotted to seize Fuxiang and welcome the Prince of Rencheng at Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: The former chief clerk Zhao Mu, the aide Wang Dangwan, and others plotted to seize Fuxiang and welcome the Prince of Rencheng at Ying.

sentences.zh: 事不果，迎紹義。

translations.literal: The affair did not succeed, so they welcomed Shaoyi instead.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed, they welcomed Shaoyi instead.

sentences.zh: 紹義至馬邑。

translations.literal: Shaoyi arrived at Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi reached Mayi.

sentences.zh: 輔相及其屬韓阿各奴等數十人，皆齊叛臣，自肆州以北城戍二百八十餘，盡從輔相，及紹義至，皆反焉。

translations.literal: Fuxiang and his followers Han Agennu and several dozen others were all Qi turncoats; from Sizhou northward more than two hundred eighty walled posts all followed Fuxiang, and when Shaoyi arrived they all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxiang and his followers Han Agennu and several dozen others were all Qi defectors. From Sizhou northward, more than two hundred and eighty garrison posts followed Fuxiang, and when Shaoyi arrived they all rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 紹義與靈州刺史袁洪猛引兵南出，欲取并州。

translations.literal: Shaoyi and the Governor of Ling Province Yuan Hongmeng led troops south, intending to take Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi and Governor Yuan Hongmeng of Ling led troops south, intending to retake Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 至新興而肆州已為周守，前隊二儀同以所部降周。

translations.literal: When they reached Xinxing, Sizhou was already held by Zhou; the vanguard's two Commanders Unequalled in Honor surrendered their troops to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinxing they found Sizhou already in Zhou hands; two Commanders Unequalled in Honor in the vanguard surrendered their units to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周兵擊顯州，執刺史陸瓊，又攻陷諸城。

translations.literal: Zhou troops attacked Xian Province, captured Governor Lu Qiong, and also stormed several cities.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou forces attacked Xian Province, captured Governor Lu Qiong, and took several cities as well.

sentences.zh: 紹義還保北朔。

translations.literal: Shaoyi withdrew to hold Northern Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi fell back to defend Northern Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 周將宇文神舉軍逼馬邑，紹義遣杜明達拒之，兵大敗。

translations.literal: The Zhou general Yuwen Shenju pressed on Mayi with his army; Shaoyi sent Du Mingda to resist him, and the army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou general Yuwen Shenju pressed Mayi with his army. Shaoyi sent Du Mingda to resist, and his forces were routed.

sentences.zh: 紹義曰：「有死而已，不能降人。

translations.literal: Shaoyi said, "Death is all there is—I cannot submit to others.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi said, "I would rather die than surrender to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」遂奔突厥。

translations.literal: 」He then fled to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: 」He then fled among the Turks.

sentences.zh: 眾三千家，令之曰：「欲還者任意。

translations.literal: With three thousand households in his train, he told them, "Whoever wishes to return may do as he pleases.
translations.idiomatic: With three thousand households following him, he told them, "Those who wish to return may do as they please.

sentences.zh: 」於是哭拜別者大半。

translations.literal: 」Then more than half wept, bowed, and took their leave.
translations.idiomatic: 」More than half wept, bowed farewell, and departed.

sentences.zh: 突厥他缽可汗謂文宣為英雄天子，以紹義重踝似之，甚見愛重。

translations.literal: Taboch Khan of the Turks called Wensuan a heroic Son of Heaven; because Shaoyi's heavy ankles resembled his, he was greatly cherished.
translations.idiomatic: Taboch Khan of the Turks had called Emperor Wensuan a heroic Son of Heaven; finding that Shaoyi's heavy ankles resembled his, he held him in great esteem.

sentences.zh: 凡齊人在北者，悉隸紹義。

translations.literal: All Qi people in the north were placed under Shaoyi's authority.
translations.idiomatic: All Qi subjects in the north were placed under Shaoyi's command.

sentences.zh: 高寶甯在營州，表上尊號，紹義遂即皇帝位，稱武平元年，以趙穆為天水王。

translations.literal: Gao Baoning at Ying Province submitted a memorial proposing an imperial title; Shaoyi thereupon assumed the throne, taking the reign title Wuping year one, and made Zhao Mu Prince of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baoning at Ying Province submitted a memorial proposing an imperial title. Shaoyi thereupon proclaimed himself emperor, taking the reign title Wuping year one, and enfeoffed Zhao Mu as Prince of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 他缽聞寶甯得平州，亦招諸部，各舉兵南向，雲共立范陽王作齊帝，為其報仇。

translations.literal: When Taboch heard that Baoning had taken Ping Province, he too summoned the tribes, each raising troops southward, declaring that they would jointly install the Prince of Fanyang as Qi emperor and avenge him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taboch heard that Baoning had taken Ping Province, he too summoned the tribes to march south, declaring that they would install the Prince of Fanyang as Qi emperor and avenge his cause.

sentences.zh: 周武帝大集兵于雲陽，將親北伐，遇疾暴崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou massed a great army at Yunyang, intending to lead a northern campaign in person, but suddenly fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou massed a great army at Yunyang and intended to lead a northern campaign in person, but suddenly fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 紹義聞之，以為天贊己。

translations.literal: When Shaoyi heard this, he thought Heaven was aiding him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyi heard this, he took it as Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: 盧昌期據范陽，亦表迎紹義。

translations.literal: Lu Changqi held Fanyang and also submitted a memorial welcoming Shaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Changqi, holding Fanyang, also submitted a memorial welcoming Shaoyi.

sentences.zh: 俄而周將宇文神舉攻滅昌期。

translations.literal: Before long the Zhou general Yuwen Shenju attacked and extinguished Changqi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Zhou general Yuwen Shenju attacked and destroyed Changqi.

sentences.zh: 其日，紹義適至幽州，聞周總管出兵于外，欲乘虛取薊城。

translations.literal: That day Shaoyi happened to reach You Province; hearing that the Zhou commander-in-chief had led troops out, he wished to exploit the vacancy and take Ji city.
translations.idiomatic: That day Shaoyi happened to reach You Province. Hearing that the Zhou commander had marched out with his troops, he intended to exploit the opening and seize Ji.

sentences.zh: 列天子旌旗，登燕昭王塚，乘高望遠，部分兵眾。

translations.literal: He displayed the imperial banners and flags, ascended the tomb-mound of King Zhao of Yan, looked far from the height, and deployed his forces.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the imperial banners, ascended the tomb-mound of King Zhao of Yan, surveyed the land from on high, and deployed his troops.

sentences.zh: 神舉遣大將軍宇文恩將四千人馳救幽州，半為齊軍所殺。

translations.literal: Shenju sent the great general Yuwen En with four thousand men to gallop to relieve You Province; half were killed by Qi troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shenju sent the great general Yuwen En with four thousand men to gallop to the relief of You Province; half were slain by Qi forces.

sentences.zh: 紹義聞范陽城陷，素服舉哀，回軍入突厥。

translations.literal: When Shaoyi heard that Fanyang city had fallen, he put on plain mourning garb and raised a lament, then withdrew his army into the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyi learned that Fanyang had fallen, he put on mourning garb and raised a lament, then withdrew among the Turks.

sentences.zh: 周人購之於他缽，又使賀若誼往說之。

translations.literal: The Zhou people offered a reward for him to Taboch and also sent He Ruoyi to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou court offered a bounty for him to Taboch and also sent He Ruoyi to win him over.

sentences.zh: 他缽又不忍，遂偽與紹義獵于南境，使誼執之，流於蜀。

translations.literal: Taboch could not bear to do it, so he feigned a hunt with Shaoyi on the southern frontier, had Yi seize him, and had him exiled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Taboch could not bring himself to hand him over, so he feigned a hunt with Shaoyi on the southern frontier, had Yi seize him, and sent him into exile in Shu.

sentences.zh: 紹義妃，勃海封孝琬女，自突厥逃歸。

translations.literal: Shaoyi's consort, a daughter of Feng Xiaowan of Bohai, escaped from among the Turks and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi's consort, a daughter of Feng Xiaowan of Bohai, escaped from the Turks and returned home.

sentences.zh: 紹義在蜀，遺妃書云：「夷狄無信，送吾於此。

translations.literal: While Shaoyi was in Shu, he sent his consort a letter saying, "The barbarians are faithless—they have sent me here.
translations.idiomatic: While Shaoyi was in Shu, he sent his consort a letter saying, "These barbarians are faithless—they have sent me here.

sentences.zh: 」竟死蜀中。

translations.literal: 」In the end he died in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: 」He died in Shu in the end.

sentences.zh: 西河王紹仁，文宣第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Shaoren of Xihe was Wensuan's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaoren of Xihe was the fourth son of Emperor Wensuan.

sentences.zh: 天保末，為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, he was made Defender-in-Chief with Equivalence to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he held the rank of Defender-in-Chief with Equivalence to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 尋薨。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 隴西王紹廉，文宣第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Shaolian of Longxi was Wensuan's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaolian of Longxi was the fifth son of Emperor Wensuan.

sentences.zh: 初封長樂，後改焉。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle, then the title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Changle, then given a new title.

sentences.zh: 性粗暴，嘗拔刀逐紹義，紹義走入廄，閉門拒之。

translations.literal: By nature he was violent and rough; once he drew a sword and chased Shaoyi, who ran into the stable and shut the door to keep him out.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was violent and rough. Once he drew a sword and chased Shaoyi, who fled into the stable and barred the door against him.

sentences.zh: 紹義初為清都尹，未及理事。

translations.literal: Shaoyi had just become Director of the Capital District and had not yet begun to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi had just been appointed Director of the Capital District and had not yet begun to administer affairs.

sentences.zh: 紹廉先往，喚囚悉出，率意決遣之。

translations.literal: Shaolian went ahead of him, summoned all the prisoners out, and disposed of cases as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: Shaolian went ahead of him, had all the prisoners brought out, and decided their cases as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 能飲酒，一舉數升，終以此薨。

translations.literal: He could drink wine—one draft of several sheng—and in the end died from this.
translations.idiomatic: He could hold his wine, drinking several sheng in a single draft, and in the end died of it.

sentences.zh: 孝昭七男：元皇后生樂陵王百年；

translations.literal: Xiaozhao had seven sons: the Empress of the Yuan clan bore Prince Bainian of Leling;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhao had seven sons. Empress Yuan bore Prince Bainian of Leling;

sentences.zh: 桑氏生襄城王亮，出後襄城景王；

translations.literal: Lady Sang bore Prince Liang of Xiangcheng, who was made heir to Prince Jing of Xiangcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Sang bore Prince Liang of Xiangcheng, who was adopted as heir to Prince Jing of Xiangcheng;

sentences.zh: 諸姬生汝南王彥理、始平王彥德、城陽王彥基、定陽王彥康、汝陽王彥忠。

translations.literal: the various consorts bore Prince Yanli of Runan, Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: his other consorts bore Prince Yanli of Runan, Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 河清三年五月，白虹圍日再重，又橫貫而不達；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Heqing, a white rainbow encircled the sun twice, and also ran horizontally across without reaching it;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Heqing, a white rainbow encircled the sun twice and also ran horizontally across it without completing the passage;

sentences.zh: 赤星見，帝以盆水承星影而蓋之，一夜盆自破。

translations.literal: a red star appeared; the emperor caught its reflection in a basin of water and covered it, but overnight the basin broke of itself.
translations.idiomatic: a red star appeared. The emperor caught its reflection in a basin of water and covered it, but overnight the basin broke of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 欲以百年厭之。

translations.literal: He wished to use Bainian to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: He intended to use Bainian to counter the omen.

sentences.zh: 會博陵人賈德胄教百年書，百年嘗作數敕字，德胄封以奏。

translations.literal: It happened that Jia Dezhao of Boling taught Bainian writing; Bainian once wrote several characters of an edict, and Dezhao sealed them and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Jia Dezhao of Boling was teaching Bainian to write. Bainian once penned several characters in the style of an edict, and Dezhao sealed the sheet and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 帝發怒，使召百年。

translations.literal: The emperor flew into a rage and had Bainian summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and summoned Bainian.

sentences.zh: 百年被召，自知不免，割帶玦，留與妃斛律氏。

translations.literal: When Bainian was summoned, knowing he could not escape, he cut off his belt pendant and left it for his consort, Lady Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to appear, Bainian knew he could not escape. He cut off his belt pendant and left it for his consort, Lady Hulu.

sentences.zh: 見帝于玄都苑涼風堂。

translations.literal: He saw the emperor in the Hall of Cool Breeze in the Mystic Capital Park.
translations.idiomatic: He appeared before the emperor in the Hall of Cool Breeze in the Mystic Capital Park.

sentences.zh: 使百年書敕字，驗與德胄所奏相似。

translations.literal: The emperor had Bainian write the edict characters; they matched what Dezhao had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Bainian write the edict characters, and they matched what Dezhao had submitted.

sentences.zh: 遣左右亂捶擊之，又令人曳百年繞堂，且走且打，所過處，血皆遍地。

translations.literal: He sent attendants to beat him at random, then had men drag Bainian around the hall, striking him as he went; wherever he passed, blood covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He had attendants beat him at random, then had men drag Bainian around the hall, striking him as he went until blood covered the floor wherever he passed.

sentences.zh: 氣息將盡，曰：「乞命，願與阿叔作奴。

translations.literal: When his breath was nearly gone, he said, "I beg for my life—I wish to be a slave to Uncle.
translations.idiomatic: As his breath failed, he pleaded, "Spare my life—I will be Uncle's slave.

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之，棄諸池，池水盡赤，於後園親看埋之。

translations.literal: 」He was then beheaded and thrown into a pool; the pool water turned entirely red, and in the rear garden the emperor personally watched as he was buried.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was then beheaded and thrown into a pool until the water ran red; in the rear garden the emperor personally watched as he was buried.

sentences.zh: 妃把玦哀號，不肯食，月餘亦死。

translations.literal: The consort clutched the pendant and wailed, refusing food; after more than a month she too died.
translations.idiomatic: His consort clutched the pendant and wailed, refusing to eat; after more than a month she too died.

sentences.zh: 玦猶在手，拳不可開，時年十四。

translations.literal: The pendant was still in her hand; her fist could not be opened—she was then fourteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: The pendant was still clenched in her hand and her fist would not open. She was fourteen years old.

sentences.zh: 其父光自擘之，乃開。

translations.literal: Her father Guang pried it open himself, and only then did it open.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Guang pried it open himself before it would release.
