sentences.zh: 後主時，改九院為二十七院，掘得小屍，緋袍金帶，一髻一解，一足有靴。

translations.literal: During the Last Ruler's reign the nine courtyards were changed to twenty-seven courtyards; a small corpse was dug up, in a crimson robe with a gold belt, one topknot undone, one foot still shod.
translations.idiomatic: During the Last Ruler's reign the nine courtyards were expanded to twenty-seven, and a small corpse was unearthed in a crimson robe with a gold belt, one topknot undone and one foot still booted.

sentences.zh: 諸內參竅言，百年太子也。

translations.literal: The palace attendants whispered that it was Crown Prince Bainian.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants whispered that it was Crown Prince Bainian.

sentences.zh: 或以為太原王紹德。

translations.literal: Some thought it was Prince Shaode of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Others thought it was Prince Shaode of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 詔以襄城王子白澤襲爵樂陵王。

translations.literal: An edict made Prince Baize of Xiangcheng the heir and successor to the title Prince of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Prince Baize of Xiangcheng as heir to succeed to the title Prince of Leling.

sentences.zh: 齊亡入關，徙蜀死。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he entered the Pass and was transferred to Shu, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he was taken west of the Pass and transferred to Shu, where he died.

sentences.zh: 始平王彥德、城陽王彥基、定陽王彥康、汝陽王彥忠與汝南王同受封，並加儀同三司，後事闕。

translations.literal: Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang received enfeoffment together with the Prince of Runan and were all given Equivalence to the Three Excellencies; later events are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yande of Shiping, Prince Yanji of Chengyang, Prince Yankang of Dingyang, and Prince Yanzhong of Ruyang were enfeoffed together with the Prince of Runan, all receiving Equivalence to the Three Excellencies; their later careers are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 武成十三男：胡皇后生後主及琅邪王儼；

translations.literal: Wucheng had thirteen sons: Empress Hu bore the Last Ruler and Prince Yan of Langye;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng had thirteen sons. Empress Hu bore the Last Ruler and Prince Yan of Langye;

sentences.zh: 李夫人生南陽王綽；

translations.literal: Lady Li bore Prince Chuo of Nanyang;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li, a consort, bore Prince Chuo of Nanyang;

sentences.zh: 後宮生齊安王廓、北平王貞、高平王仁英、淮南王仁光、西河王仁機、樂平王仁邕、潁川王仁儉、安樂王仁雅、丹楊王仁直、東海王仁謙。

translations.literal: consorts of the rear palace bore Prince Kuo of Qi'an, Prince Zhen of Beiping, Prince Renying of Gaoping, Prince Renguang of Huainan, Prince Renji of Xihe, Prince Renyong of Leping, Prince Renjian of Yingchuan, Prince Renya of Anle, Prince Renzhi of Danyang, and Prince Renqian of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: rear-palace consorts bore Prince Kuo of Qi'an, Prince Zhen of Beiping, Prince Renying of Gaoping, Prince Renguang of Huainan, Prince Renji of Xihe, Prince Renyong of Leping, Prince Renjian of Yingchuan, Prince Renya of Anle, Prince Renzhi of Danyang, and Prince Renqian of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 南陽王綽，字仁通，武成長子也。

translations.literal: Prince Chuo of Nanyang, style Rentong, was Wucheng's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chuo of Nanyang, style Rentong, was the eldest son of Emperor Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 以五月五日辰時生，至午時，後主乃生。

translations.literal: He was born on the fifth day of the fifth month at the hour of the dragon; the Last Ruler was born only at the hour of the horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on the fifth day of the fifth month at the hour of the dragon, while the Last Ruler was not born until the hour of the horse.

sentences.zh: 武成以綽母李夫人非正嫡，故貶為第二。

translations.literal: Because Chuo's mother Lady Li was not the legitimate principal consort, Wucheng demoted him to second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chuo's mother Lady Li was not the principal consort, Emperor Wucheng demoted him to second in rank.

sentences.zh: 初名融，字君明，出後漢陽王。

translations.literal: At first his name was Rong and his style Junming; he was made heir to the Prince of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was first named Rong, style Junming, and was made heir to the Prince of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 河清三年，改封南陽，別為漢陽置後。

translations.literal: In the third year of Heqing his fief was changed to Nanyang, and a separate heir was established for Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing he was transferred to Nanyang, and a separate heir was established for Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 綽始十餘歲，留守晉陽。

translations.literal: When Chuo was just over ten, he remained at Jinyang as regent.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his early teens, Chuo remained at Jinyang as regent.

sentences.zh: 愛波斯狗。

translations.literal: He loved Persian dogs.
translations.idiomatic: He doted on Persian dogs.

sentences.zh: 尉破胡諫之，欻然斫殺數狗，狼藉在地。

translations.literal: Wei Pohu remonstrated with him; in a sudden rage he hacked several dogs to death, and they lay scattered on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Pohu remonstrated with him; in a sudden fury he hacked several dogs to death until they lay scattered on the ground.

sentences.zh: 破胡驚走，不敢復言。

translations.literal: Pohu fled in alarm and did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Pohu fled in alarm and never dared speak of it again.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he served as Minister over the Masses and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Minister over the Masses and Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 好裸人，畫為獸狀，縱犬噬而食之。

translations.literal: He liked naked people, painted them in the shapes of beasts, and set dogs on them to bite and eat them.
translations.idiomatic: He took delight in naked victims, painted them to look like beasts, and set dogs on them to tear them apart and devour them.

sentences.zh: 左轉定州，汲井水為後池，在樓上彈人。

translations.literal: Transferred left to Dingzhou, he drew well water for a rear pool and from the upper story used a catapult to shoot at people.
translations.idiomatic: After his transfer to Dingzhou, he drew well water into a rear pool and from an upper story used a catapult to shoot at people below.

sentences.zh: 好微行，遊獵無度，恣情強暴，雲學文宣伯為人。

translations.literal: He loved traveling incognito, hunting without limit, indulging in violence as he pleased, and claimed to emulate Prince Wenxuan's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He loved traveling in disguise, hunted without restraint, and indulged in violence at will, claiming to take Prince Wenxuan as his model.

sentences.zh: 有婦人抱兒在路，走避入草，綽奪其兒飼波斯狗。

translations.literal: A woman carrying a child was on the road; fleeing into the grass to escape, Chuo seized her child and fed it to his Persian dog.
translations.idiomatic: A woman carrying a child was on the road. As she fled into the grass to escape, Chuo snatched her child and fed it to his Persian dog.

sentences.zh: 婦人號哭，綽怒，又縱狗使食，狗不食，塗以兒血，乃食焉。

translations.literal: The woman wailed; Chuo grew angry, set the dog on her again to eat, but the dog would not eat until smeared with the child's blood, and only then did it eat.
translations.idiomatic: The woman wailed in grief. Chuo flew into a rage and set the dog on her again, but the dog would not eat until he smeared it with the child's blood—only then would it feed.

sentences.zh: 後主聞之，詔鎖綽赴行在所。

translations.literal: The Last Ruler heard of it and issued an edict to shackle Chuo and bring him to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Ruler heard of this, he ordered Chuo shackled and brought to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 至而宥之，問在州何者最樂。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor pardoned him and asked what had pleased him most in the province.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuo arrived, the emperor pardoned him and asked what had given him the greatest pleasure in the province.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「多取鲩歇，將蛆混看，極樂。

translations.literal: He replied, "Taking much putrid fish scraps and mixing them with maggots to watch is supreme delight.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Gathering great heaps of putrid fish scraps and mixing them with maggots to watch—that is supreme delight.

sentences.zh: 」後主即夜索鲩歇一斗，比曉，得二三升，置諸浴斛，使人裸臥浴斛中，號叫宛轉。

translations.literal: That very night the Last Ruler sought a peck of putrid fish scraps; by dawn only two or three sheng had been obtained. These were placed in a bathing tub, and a man was made to lie naked in it, wailing and writhing.
translations.idiomatic: That very night the Last Ruler sent for a peck of putrid fish scraps. By dawn only two or three sheng had been found. They were placed in a bathing tub, and a man was made to lie naked inside it, wailing and writhing in agony.

sentences.zh: 帝與綽臨觀，喜噱不已。

translations.literal: The emperor and Chuo watched from above, laughing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Chuo looked on, roaring with laughter without end.

sentences.zh: 謂綽曰：「如此樂事，何不早馳驛奏聞？

translations.literal: He said to Chuo, "For such a delightful amusement, why did you not earlier dispatch a courier to report it?
translations.idiomatic: He said to Chuo, "For such a delightful amusement, why did you not send a courier posthaste to tell me sooner?

sentences.zh: 」綽由是大為後主寵，拜大將軍，朝夕同戲。

translations.literal: From this Chuo came to be greatly favored by the Last Ruler, was appointed Grand General, and day and night played together with him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Chuo won the Last Ruler's great favor. He was appointed Grand General and spent every day and night at play with him.

sentences.zh: 韓長鸞間之，除齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Han Changluan slandered him, and he was dismissed to serve as Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Changluan slandered him, and he was transferred to serve as Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 將發，長鸞令綽親信誣告其反，奏云：「此犯國法，不可赦。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Changluan had Chuo's trusted followers falsely accuse him of rebellion, memorializing, "This man has violated the laws of the state and cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Just before his departure, Changluan had Chuo's trusted followers falsely accuse him of rebellion, memorializing, "This man has violated the laws of the state and cannot be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」後主不忍顯戮，使寵胡何猥薩後園與綽相撲，扼殺之。

translations.literal: The Last Ruler could not bear a public execution and had his favored Hu attendant He Weisa wrestle with Chuo in the rear garden and strangle him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Ruler could not bear a public execution and had his favored Hu attendant He Weisa wrestle with Chuo in the rear garden and strangle him.

sentences.zh: 瘞於興聖佛寺，經四百餘日乃大斂，顏色毛髮皆如生。

translations.literal: He was buried at Xingsheng Buddhist Temple; only after more than four hundred days was the full funeral rite performed, and his complexion and hair were as in life.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Xingsheng Buddhist Temple. Only after more than four hundred days was the full funeral rite performed, and his complexion and hair were still as in life.

sentences.zh: 俗雲五月五日生者，腦不壞。

translations.literal: Popular lore says that one born on the fifth day of the fifth month does not decay in the brain.
translations.idiomatic: Popular lore held that anyone born on the fifth day of the fifth month would not decay in the brain.

sentences.zh: 綽兄弟皆呼父為兄兄，嫡母為家家，乳母為姊姊，婦為妹妹。

translations.literal: Chuo and his brothers all called their father "elder brother," the principal mother "jiajia," the wet nurse "elder sister," and their wives "younger sister."
translations.idiomatic: Chuo and his brothers all called their father "elder brother," the principal mother "jiajia," the wet nurse "elder sister," and their wives "younger sister."

sentences.zh: 齊亡，妃鄭氏為周武帝所幸，請葬綽，敕所司葬于永平陵北。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, his consort Lady Zheng won the favor of Emperor Wu of Zhou; she requested burial for Chuo, and an edict ordered the authorities to bury him north of Yongping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, his consort Lady Zheng won the favor of Emperor Wu of Zhou. She requested burial for Chuo, and an edict ordered the authorities to bury him north of Yongping Tomb.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王儼字仁威，武成第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince Yan of Langye, style Renwei, was Wucheng's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan of Langye, style Renwei, was the third son of Emperor Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 初封東平王，拜開府、侍中、中書監、京畿大都督、領軍大將軍，領御史中丞。

translations.literal: At first enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping, he was appointed Opener of a Government Office, Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, Grand Commander of the Capital Region, General-in-Chief of the Palace Guard, and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping and appointed Opener of a Government Office, Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, Grand Commander of the Capital Region, General-in-Chief of the Palace Guard, and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 遷大司徒、尚書令、大將軍、錄尚書事、大司馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister over the Masses, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand General, Recorder of Affairs in the Department of State Affairs, and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister over the Masses, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand General, Recorder of Affairs in the Department of State Affairs, and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 魏氏舊制，中丞出，千步清道，與皇太子分路行，王公皆遙住車，去牛頓軛於地，以待中丞過。

translations.literal: Under the old Wei system, when the Censor-in-Chief went out, the road was cleared for a thousand paces; he traveled by a separate route from the Crown Prince, and princes and nobles all halted their carriages at a distance, removed the oxen and set the yokes on the ground, and waited for the Censor-in-Chief to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Wei system, when the Censor-in-Chief went abroad the road was cleared for a thousand paces. He traveled by a separate route from the Crown Prince, and princes and nobles all halted their carriages at a distance, unyoked their oxen, and waited for the Censor-in-Chief to pass.

sentences.zh: 其或遲違，則赤棒棒之。

translations.literal: If anyone was slow or disobedient, he was beaten with the red staff.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who was slow or disobedient was beaten with the red staff.

sentences.zh: 自都鄴後，此儀浸絕。

translations.literal: After the capital was established at Ye, this ceremony gradually died out.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was moved to Ye, this ceremony gradually fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 武成欲雄寵儼，乃使一依舊制。

translations.literal: Wucheng wished to show Yan off in full majesty and had the old system followed in every detail.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng wished to display Yan in full majesty and had the old system restored in every detail.

sentences.zh: 儼初從北宮出，將上中丞，凡京畿步騎，領軍之官屬，中丞之威儀，司徒之鹵簿，莫不畢備。

translations.literal: When Yan first went out from the Northern Palace to assume the post of Censor-in-Chief, all the infantry and cavalry of the capital region, the officers of the Palace Guard, the Censor-in-Chief's guard of honor, and the Minister over the Masses' full retinue were completely assembled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan first went out from the Northern Palace to assume the post of Censor-in-Chief, all the infantry and cavalry of the capital region, the officers of the Palace Guard, the Censor-in-Chief's guard of honor, and the Minister over the Masses' full retinue were completely assembled.

sentences.zh: 帝與胡後在華林園東門外，張幕隔青紗步障觀之。

translations.literal: The emperor and Empress Hu were outside the east gate of Hualin Garden, watching from behind curtains and green gauze screens.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Empress Hu watched from outside the east gate of Hualin Garden, seated behind curtains and green gauze screens.

sentences.zh: 遣中貴驟馬趣仗，不得入，自言奉敕，赤棒應聲碎其鞍，馬驚人墜。

translations.literal: He sent a palace eunuch galloping to join the guard formation, but entry was denied; claiming he came by imperial order, the red staff instantly shattered his saddle, the horse bolted, and the man fell.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a palace eunuch galloping to join the guard formation, but entry was denied. When the man claimed he came by imperial order, a red staff instantly shattered his saddle; the horse bolted and he was thrown to the ground.

sentences.zh: 帝大笑，以為善。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly and considered it excellent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily and approved.

sentences.zh: 更敕令駐車，傳語良久，觀者傾京邑。

translations.literal: He then ordered the carriage to halt and exchanged words at length; onlookers filled the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the carriage to halt and exchanged words at length, and onlookers filled the entire capital.

sentences.zh: 儼恆在宮中，坐含章殿以視事，諸父皆拜焉。

translations.literal: Yan constantly remained in the palace, holding court in Hanzhang Hall, and all his uncles bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan constantly remained in the palace, holding court in Hanzhang Hall, and all his uncles bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 帝幸并州，儼恆居守。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Bingzhou, Yan always remained behind as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor visited Bingzhou, Yan remained behind as regent.

sentences.zh: 每送駕，或半路，或至晉陽乃還。

translations.literal: Each time he escorted the imperial procession, he would turn back either halfway or only upon reaching Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he escorted the imperial procession, he would turn back either halfway or only after reaching Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 王師羅嘗從駕，後至，武成欲罪之。

translations.literal: Wang Shiluo once accompanied the imperial procession but arrived late; Wucheng wished to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiluo once accompanied the imperial procession but arrived late, and Emperor Wucheng wished to punish him.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「臣與第三子別，留連不覺晚。

translations.literal: He pleaded, "Your servant parted from the Third Son and lingered so long that I did not notice how late it had grown.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded, "Your servant parted from the Third Son and lingered so long that I did not notice how late it had grown.

sentences.zh: 」武成憶儼，為之下泣，舍師羅不問。

translations.literal: Wucheng thought of Yan and wept for it; he released Shiluo without further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng thought of Yan and wept; he released Shiluo without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 儼器服玩飾皆與後主同，所須悉官給。

translations.literal: Yan's vessels, robes, ornaments, and playthings were all the same as the Last Ruler's, and everything he needed was supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's vessels, robes, ornaments, and playthings were all identical to the Last Ruler's, and everything he needed was supplied by the state.

sentences.zh: 于南宮嘗見新冰綠李，還，怒曰：「尊兄已有，我何意無？

translations.literal: In the Southern Palace he once saw fresh ice and green plums; returning, he said angrily, "My elder brother already has them—why should I not?
translations.idiomatic: In the Southern Palace he once saw fresh ice and green plums. Returning, he said angrily, "My elder brother already has them—why should I not?

sentences.zh: 」從是，後主先得新奇，屬官及工匠必獲罪。

translations.literal: From then on the Last Ruler always received novelties first, and subordinate officials and artisans were invariably punished.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Last Ruler always received novelties first, and subordinate officials and artisans were invariably punished.

sentences.zh: 太上、胡後猶以為不足。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor and Empress Hu still thought this insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor and Empress Hu still thought this insufficient.

sentences.zh: 儼嘗患喉，使醫下針，張目不瞬。

translations.literal: Yan once suffered from the throat and had a physician insert a needle; he kept his eyes open without blinking.
translations.idiomatic: Yan once suffered from a throat ailment and had a physician insert a needle; he kept his eyes open without blinking.

sentences.zh: 又言於帝曰：「阿兄軟，何能率左右！

translations.literal: He also said to the emperor, "Elder brother is soft—how can he command those around him!
translations.idiomatic: He also said to the emperor, "Elder brother is soft—how can he command those around him!

sentences.zh: 」帝每稱曰：「此黠兒也，當有所成。

translations.literal: The emperor always praised him, saying, "This clever boy will surely achieve something.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always praised him, saying, "This clever boy will surely achieve something.

sentences.zh: 」以後主為劣，有廢立之意。

translations.literal: He considered the Last Ruler inferior and had thoughts of deposing and replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: He considered the Last Ruler inferior and entertained thoughts of deposing and replacing him.

sentences.zh: 武成崩，改封琅邪。

translations.literal: When Wucheng died, his fief was changed to Langye.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wucheng died, Yan's fief was changed to Langye.

sentences.zh: 儼以和士開、駱提婆等奢恣，盛修第宅，意甚不平。

translations.literal: Yan resented He Shikai, Luo Tipo, and others for their extravagant indulgence and lavish building of mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Yan resented He Shikai, Luo Tipo, and others for their extravagant indulgence and lavish building of mansions.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂曰：「君等所營宅，早晚當就，何太遲也？

translations.literal: He once said to them, "The mansions you are building should be finished soon or late—why so slow?
translations.idiomatic: He once said to them, "The mansions you are building should be finished before long—why so slow?

sentences.zh: 」二人相謂曰：「琅邪王眼光弈弈，數步射人，向者暫對，不覺汗出。

translations.literal: The two said to each other, "Prince Yan of Langye's eyes gleam sharply; from several paces they pierce a man. Just now, facing him briefly, we broke out in sweat without noticing.
translations.idiomatic: The two said to each other, "Prince Yan of Langye's eyes gleam sharply; from several paces they pierce a man. Just now, facing him briefly, we broke out in sweat without noticing.

sentences.zh: 天子門奏事，尚不然。

translations.literal: Even when presenting business at the Son of Heaven's gate it is not like this.
translations.idiomatic: Even when presenting business at the Son of Heaven's gate it is not like this.

sentences.zh: 」由是忌之。

translations.literal: From this they came to fear and resent him.
translations.idiomatic: From this they came to fear and resent him.

sentences.zh: 武平二年，出儼居北宮，五日一朝，不復得無時見太后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuping, Yan was moved out to reside in the Northern Palace, attending court once every five days, and no longer allowed to see the Empress Dowager at any time.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuping, Yan was moved out to reside in the Northern Palace, attending court once every five days, and no longer allowed to see the Empress Dowager at will.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔除太保，余官悉解，猶帶中丞，且京畿。

translations.literal: In the fourth month an edict removed him as Grand Guardian; all other offices were dismissed, though he still held the post of Censor-in-Chief over the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month an edict removed him as Grand Guardian; all other offices were dismissed, though he still held the post of Censor-in-Chief over the capital region.

sentences.zh: 以北城有武庫，欲移儼於外，然後奪其兵權。

translations.literal: Because the northern city held the armory, they wished to move Yan outside and then strip him of military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Because the northern city held the armory, they wished to move Yan outside the walls and then strip him of military authority.

sentences.zh: 書侍御史王子宜與儼左右開府高舍洛、中常侍劉辟強說儼曰：「殿下被疏，正由士開間構，何可出北宮，入百姓叢中也？

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wang Ziyi, together with Yan's attendants Opener of a Government Office Gao Sheluo and Palace Attendant Liu Biqiang, urged Yan, saying, "Your Highness has been estranged precisely because of He Shikai's slander—how can you leave the Northern Palace and enter the midst of common people?
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wang Ziyi, together with Yan's attendants Opener of a Government Office Gao Sheluo and Palace Attendant Liu Biqiang, urged Yan, saying, "Your Highness has been estranged precisely because of He Shikai's slander—how can you leave the Northern Palace and enter the midst of common people?

sentences.zh: 」儼謂侍中馮子琮曰：「士開罪重，兒欲殺之。

translations.literal: Yan said to Palace Attendant Feng Zicong, "He Shikai's crimes are grave; I wish to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said to Palace Attendant Feng Zicong, "He Shikai's crimes are grave; I wish to kill him.

sentences.zh: 」子琮心欲廢帝而立儼，因贊成其事。

translations.literal: Zicong inwardly wished to depose the emperor and establish Yan, and therefore encouraged the deed.
translations.idiomatic: Zicong inwardly wished to depose the emperor and establish Yan, and therefore encouraged the deed.

sentences.zh: 儼乃令子宜表彈士開罪，請付禁推。

translations.literal: Yan then had Ziyi memorialize impeaching He Shikai's crimes and request that he be handed over for imprisonment and investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then had Ziyi memorialize impeaching He Shikai's crimes and request that he be handed over for imprisonment and investigation.

sentences.zh: 子琮雜以他文書奏之，後主不審省而可之。

translations.literal: Zicong mixed it with other documents in the memorial; the Last Ruler did not examine it closely and approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Zicong mixed it with other documents in the memorial; the Last Ruler did not examine it closely and approved it.

sentences.zh: 儼誑領軍厙狄伏連曰：「奉敕，令領軍收士開。

translations.literal: Yan deceived General-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Kudie Fulian, saying, "By imperial order, the General-in-Chief is to arrest He Shikai.
translations.idiomatic: Yan deceived General-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Kudie Fulian, saying, "By imperial order, the General-in-Chief is to arrest He Shikai.

sentences.zh: 」伏連以諮子琮，且請覆奏。

translations.literal: Fulian consulted Zicong and also requested confirmation by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Fulian consulted Zicong and also requested confirmation by memorial.

sentences.zh: 子琮曰：「琅邪王受敕，何須重奏。

translations.literal: Zicong said, "Prince Yan of Langye has received the order—what need is there to memorialize again?
translations.idiomatic: Zicong said, "Prince Yan of Langye has received the order—what need is there to memorialize again?

sentences.zh: 」伏連信之，伏五十人於神獸門外，詰旦，執士開送御史。

translations.literal: Fulian believed him, hid fifty men outside the Divine Beast Gate, and at dawn seized He Shikai and sent him to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Fulian believed him, hid fifty men outside the Divine Beast Gate, and at dawn seized He Shikai and sent him to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 儼使馮永洛就台斬之。

translations.literal: Yan sent Feng Yongluo to the Censorate to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Feng Yongluo to the Censorate to behead him.

sentences.zh: 儼徒本意唯殺士開。

translations.literal: Yan's followers had originally intended only to kill He Shikai.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's followers had originally intended only to kill He Shikai.

sentences.zh: 及是，因逼儼曰：「事既然，不可中止。

translations.literal: At this point they pressed Yan, saying, "The affair having come this far, it cannot be halted.
translations.idiomatic: At this point they pressed Yan, saying, "The affair having come this far, it cannot be halted.

sentences.zh: 」儼遂率京畿軍士三千餘人，屯千秋門外。

translations.literal: Yan then led more than three thousand capital-region soldiers and encamped outside the Qianqiu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then led more than three thousand capital-region soldiers and encamped outside the Qianqiu Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝使劉桃枝將禁兵八十人召儼。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Liu Taozhi with eighty palace guards to summon Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Liu Taozhi with eighty palace guards to summon Yan.

sentences.zh: 桃枝遙拜，儼命反縛，將斬之，禁兵散走。

translations.literal: Taozhi bowed from afar; Yan ordered him bound hand and foot and was about to behead him, and the palace guards scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Taozhi bowed from afar. Yan ordered him bound hand and foot and was about to behead him, and the palace guards scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝又使馮子琮召儼。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Feng Zicong to summon Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Feng Zicong to summon Yan.

sentences.zh: 儼辭曰：「士開昔來實合萬死，謀廢至尊，剃家家頭使作阿尼，故擁兵馬，欲坐著孫鳳珍宅上。

translations.literal: Yan declined, saying, "He Shikai in the past truly deserved ten thousand deaths; he plotted to depose the Supreme Sovereign and shave jiajia's head to make her a nun. For this reason I gathered troops and horses, intending to take up residence in Sun Fengzhen's house.
translations.idiomatic: Yan declined, saying, "He Shikai in the past truly deserved ten thousand deaths. He plotted to depose the Supreme Sovereign and shave jiajia's head to make her a nun. For this reason I gathered troops and horses, intending to take up residence in Sun Fengzhen's house.

sentences.zh: 臣為是，矯詔誅之。

translations.literal: Your servant did this and, by forged edict, executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant did this and, by forged edict, executed him.

sentences.zh: 尊兄若欲殺臣，不敢逃罪；

translations.literal: If my elder brother wishes to kill your servant, I dare not flee punishment;
translations.idiomatic: If my elder brother wishes to kill your servant, I dare not flee punishment;

sentences.zh: 若放臣，願遣姊姊來迎臣，臣即入見。

translations.literal: if he releases your servant, I wish that elder sister be sent to receive me, and your servant will then enter to have audience.
translations.idiomatic: if he releases your servant, I wish that elder sister be sent to receive me, and your servant will then enter to have audience.

sentences.zh: 」姊姊即陸令萱也，儼欲誘出殺之。

translations.literal: Elder sister was Lu Lingxuan; Yan wished to lure her out and kill her.
translations.idiomatic: Elder sister was Lu Lingxuan; Yan wished to lure her out and kill her.

sentences.zh: 令萱執刀帝后，聞之戰慄。

translations.literal: Lingxuan held a knife to the emperor and empress; hearing this, they trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxuan held a knife to the emperor and empress; hearing this, they trembled in fear.

sentences.zh: 又使韓長鸞召儼。

translations.literal: They again sent Han Changluan to summon Yan.
translations.idiomatic: They again sent Han Changluan to summon Yan.

sentences.zh: 儼將入，劉辟強牽衣諫曰：「若不斬提婆母子，殿下無由得入。

translations.literal: As Yan was about to enter, Liu Biqiang seized his robe and remonstrated, saying, "Unless Tipo and his mother are beheaded, Your Highness will have no way to enter.
translations.idiomatic: As Yan was about to enter, Liu Biqiang seized his robe and remonstrated, saying, "Unless Tipo and his mother are beheaded, Your Highness will have no way to enter.

sentences.zh: 」廣甯、安德二王適從西來，欲助成其事，曰：「何不入？

translations.literal: The two princes, Guangning and Ande, happened to come from the west wishing to help accomplish the affair, and said, "Why not enter?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaohang of Guangning and Prince Ande happened to come from the west wishing to help accomplish the affair, and said, "Why not enter?

sentences.zh: 」辟強曰：「人少。

translations.literal: Biqiang said, "Our men are too few.
translations.idiomatic: Biqiang said, "Our men are too few.

sentences.zh: 」安德王顧眾而言曰：「孝昭殺楊遵彥，止八十人，今乃數千，何言人少？

translations.literal: Prince Ande looked at the crowd and said, "When Xiaozhao killed Yang Zunyan, he had only eighty men; now we number in the thousands—how can you say our men are too few?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ande looked at the crowd and said, "When Emperor Xiaozhao killed Yang Zunyan, he had only eighty men; now we number in the thousands—how can you say our men are too few?

sentences.zh: 」後主泣啟太后曰：「有緣，更見家家，無緣，永別。

translations.literal: The Last Ruler wept and reported to the Empress Dowager, saying, "If fate allows, I shall see jiajia again; if not, this is eternal parting.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Ruler wept and reported to the Empress Dowager, saying, "If fate allows, I shall see jiajia again; if not, this is eternal parting.

sentences.zh: 」乃急召斛律光，儼亦召之。

translations.literal: They then urgently summoned Hulu Guang; Yan summoned him as well.
translations.idiomatic: They then urgently summoned Hulu Guang; Yan summoned him as well.

sentences.zh: 光聞殺士開，撫掌大笑曰：「龍子作事，固自不似凡人。

translations.literal: Guang heard that He Shikai had been killed, clapped his hands, and laughed greatly, saying, "A dragon's son acts—naturally he is not like ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Guang heard that He Shikai had been killed, clapped his hands, and laughed heartily, saying, "A dragon's son acts—naturally he is not like ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 」入見後主於永巷。

translations.literal: He entered to see the Last Ruler in Yong Lane.
translations.idiomatic: He entered to see the Last Ruler in Yong Lane.

sentences.zh: 帝率宿衛者步騎四百，授甲將出。

translations.literal: The emperor led four hundred infantry and cavalry of the palace guard, armed them, and was about to go out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led four hundred infantry and cavalry of the palace guard, armed them, and was about to go out.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「小兒輩弄兵，與交手，即亂。

translations.literal: Guang said, "These boys are playing with arms; if you cross swords with them, there will be chaos at once.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "These boys are playing with arms; if you cross swords with them, there will be chaos at once.

sentences.zh: 鄙諺云：'奴見大家心死。

translations.literal: A vulgar proverb says, 'When a slave sees the master, his heart dies.
translations.idiomatic: A vulgar proverb says, 'When a slave sees the master, his heart dies.

sentences.zh: '至尊宜自至千秋門，琅邪必不敢動。

translations.literal: The Supreme Sovereign should go in person to the Qianqiu Gate; Prince Yan of Langye will surely not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Sovereign should go in person to the Qianqiu Gate; Prince Yan of Langye will surely not dare move.

sentences.zh: 」皮景和亦以為然，後主從之。

translations.literal: Pi Jinghe also thought this correct, and the Last Ruler followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Pi Jinghe also thought this correct, and the Last Ruler followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 光步道，使人走出曰：「大家來。

translations.literal: Guang walked on foot and had a man run out, saying, "The master comes.
translations.idiomatic: Guang walked on foot and had a man run out, saying, "The master comes.

sentences.zh: 」儼徒駭散。

translations.literal: Yan's followers were terrified and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's followers were terrified and scattered.

sentences.zh: 帝駐馬橋上，遙呼之，儼猶立不進。

translations.literal: The emperor halted his horse on the bridge and called to him from afar; Yan still stood and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted his horse on the bridge and called to him from afar; Yan still stood and did not advance.

sentences.zh: 光就謂曰：「天子弟殺一漢，何苦？

translations.literal: Guang went up to him and said, "The Son of Heaven's younger brother killed one commoner—why such distress?
translations.idiomatic: Guang went up to him and said, "The Son of Heaven's younger brother killed one commoner—why such distress?

sentences.zh: 」執其手，強引以前。

translations.literal: He seized his hand and forcibly pulled him forward.
translations.idiomatic: He seized his hand and forcibly pulled him forward.

sentences.zh: 請帝曰：「琅邪王年少，腸肥腦滿，輕為舉措，長大自不復然，願寬其罪。

translations.literal: He petitioned the emperor, saying, "Prince Yan of Langye is young, fat of belly and full of brain, and acts lightly; when he grows up he will no longer be so—I beg that his crime be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the emperor, saying, "Prince Yan of Langye is young, fat of belly and full of brain, and acts rashly; when he grows up he will no longer be so—I beg that his crime be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 」帝拔儼帶刀環，亂築辮頭，良久乃釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor drew the ring of Yan's girdle knife and beat his braided hair at random; only after a long while did he release him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drew the ring of Yan's girdle knife and beat his braided hair at random; only after a long while did he release him.

sentences.zh: 收伏連及高舍洛、王子宜、劉辟強、都督翟顯貴于後園，帝親射之而後斬，皆支解，暴之都街下。

translations.literal: Fulian, Gao Sheluo, Wang Ziyi, Liu Biqiang, and Commander Zhai Xiangui were seized in the rear garden; the emperor personally shot them and then beheaded them. All were dismembered and exposed beneath the capital's main street.
translations.idiomatic: Fulian, Gao Sheluo, Wang Ziyi, Liu Biqiang, and Commander Zhai Xiangui were seized in the rear garden. The emperor personally shot them and then beheaded them. All were dismembered and exposed beneath the capital's main street.

sentences.zh: 文武職吏，盡欲殺之。

translations.literal: All civil and military officials and clerks—they wished to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: They wished to kill all the civil and military officials and clerks involved.

sentences.zh: 光以皆勳貴子弟，恐人心不安，趙彥深亦云「《春秋》責帥」，於是罪之各有差。

translations.literal: Guang, because they were all sons of meritorious nobles, feared popular unrest; Zhao Yanshen also cited the *Spring and Autumn* dictum that "the commander is held responsible," and so their punishments were graded accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Guang, because they were all sons of meritorious nobles, feared popular unrest; Zhao Yanshen also cited the *Spring and Autumn* dictum that "the commander is held responsible," and so their punishments were graded accordingly.

sentences.zh: 儼之未獲罪也。

translations.literal: Before Yan had yet been punished for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yan had yet been punished for his crime,

sentences.zh: 鄴北城有白馬佛塔，是石季龍為澄公所作。

translations.literal: In the northern city of Ye there was a White Horse Buddhist pagoda, built by Shi Jilong for Master Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the northern city of Ye there was a White Horse Buddhist pagoda, built by Shi Jilong for Master Cheng.

sentences.zh: 儼將修之，巫曰：「若動此浮圖，此城失主。

translations.literal: Yan was about to repair it when a shaman said, "If this stupa is moved, this city will lose its lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was about to repair it when a shaman said, "If this stupa is moved, this city will lose its lord.

sentences.zh: 」不從，破至第二級，得白蛇，長數丈，迴旋失之。

translations.literal: He did not listen, broke through to the second tier, found a white serpent several zhang long, and it coiled away and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: He did not listen, broke through to the second tier, found a white serpent several zhang long, and it coiled away and vanished.

sentences.zh: 數旬而敗。

translations.literal: Within several tens of days he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Within several tens of days he was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 自是，太后處儼于宮內，食必自嘗之。

translations.literal: From then on the Empress Dowager kept Yan within the palace and always tasted his food herself first.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Empress Dowager kept Yan within the palace and always tasted his food herself before he ate.

sentences.zh: 陸令萱說帝曰：「人稱琅邪王聰明雄勇，當今無敵，觀其根表，殆非人臣。

translations.literal: Lu Lingxuan urged the emperor, saying, "People call Prince Yan of Langye clever and heroically brave, unmatched in the present age; judging from his essential bearing, he is scarcely fit to remain a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan urged the emperor, saying, "People call Prince Yan of Langye clever and heroically brave, unmatched in the present age. Judging from his essential bearing, he is scarcely fit to remain a subject.

sentences.zh: 自專殺以來，常懷恐懼，宜早為計。

translations.literal: Since the unauthorized killing, he has constantly lived in fear; you should plan early.
translations.idiomatic: Since the unauthorized killing, he has constantly lived in fear. You should act early.

sentences.zh: 」何洪珍與和士開素善，亦請殺之。

translations.literal: He Hongzhen, who had long been on good terms with He Shikai, also requested that Yan be killed.
translations.idiomatic: He Hongzhen, who had long been on good terms with He Shikai, also requested that Yan be killed.

sentences.zh: 未決，以食輦密迎祖班問之。

translations.literal: Before a decision was made, they secretly brought Zu Ban in a food carriage to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Before a decision was made, they secretly brought Zu Ban in a food carriage to consult him.

sentences.zh: 班稱周公殺管叔，季友鴆慶父，帝納其言。

translations.literal: Ban cited the Duke of Zhou's execution of Guan Shu and Jiyou's poisoning of Qing Fu; the emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Ban cited the Duke of Zhou's execution of Guan Shu and Jiyou's poisoning of Qing Fu, and the emperor accepted his argument.

sentences.zh: 以儼之晉陽，使右衛大將軍趙元侃誘執儼。

translations.literal: Yan was sent to Jinyang, and Right Guard General Zhao Yuankan was ordered to lure and seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was sent to Jinyang, and Right Guard General Zhao Yuankan was ordered to lure and seize him.

sentences.zh: 元侃曰：「臣昔事先帝日，見先帝愛王，今寧就死，不能行。

translations.literal: Yuankan said, "When your servant formerly served the late emperor, I saw how the late emperor loved the prince. Now I would rather die than carry this out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankan said, "When I formerly served the late emperor, I saw how deeply he loved the prince. Now I would rather die than carry this out.

sentences.zh: 」帝出元侃為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor transferred Yuankan out to serve as Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor transferred Yuankan out to serve as Governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月下旬，帝啟太后曰：「明旦欲與仁威出獵，須早早還。

translations.literal: In the latter part of the ninth month the emperor reported to the Empress Dowager, saying, "Tomorrow I wish to go hunting with Renwei and must return early.
translations.idiomatic: In the latter part of the ninth month the emperor reported to the Empress Dowager, saying, "Tomorrow I wish to go hunting with Renwei and must return early.

sentences.zh: 」是夜四更，帝召儼，儼疑之。

translations.literal: That night at the fourth watch the emperor summoned Yan; Yan was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the fourth watch the emperor summoned Yan, and Yan grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 陸令萱曰：「兄兄喚，兒何不去？

translations.literal: Lu Lingxuan said, "Elder brother calls—why will you not go?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan said, "Elder brother calls—why will you not go?

sentences.zh: 」儼出至永巷，劉桃枝反接其手。

translations.literal: Yan went out to Yong Lane, and Liu Taozhi bound his hands behind his back.
translations.idiomatic: Yan went out to Yong Lane, and Liu Taozhi bound his hands behind his back.

sentences.zh: 儼呼曰：「乞見家家、尊兄！

translations.literal: Yan cried out, "I beg to see jiajia and my elder brother!
translations.idiomatic: Yan cried out, "I beg to see jiajia and my elder brother!

sentences.zh: 」桃枝以袖塞其口，反袍蒙頭負出，至大明宮，鼻血滿面，立殺之，時年十四。

translations.literal: Taozhi stuffed his mouth with a sleeve, covered his head with a reversed robe, and carried him out. At Daming Palace, with blood from his nose covering his face, he was immediately killed—he was then fourteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: Taozhi stuffed his mouth with a sleeve, covered his head with a reversed robe, and carried him out. At Daming Palace, with blood from his nose covering his face, he was immediately killed. He was fourteen years old.

sentences.zh: 不脫靴，裹以席，埋於室內。

translations.literal: Without removing his boots, they wrapped him in a mat and buried him inside the room.
translations.idiomatic: Without removing his boots, they wrapped him in a mat and buried him inside the room.

sentences.zh: 帝使啟太后，臨哭十餘聲，便擁入殿。

translations.literal: The emperor had someone report to the Empress Dowager; she wept over the body for more than ten cries, then was escorted into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had someone report to the Empress Dowager. She wept over the body for a dozen cries, then was escorted into the hall.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，葬於鄴西，贈諡曰楚恭哀帝，以慰太后。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year he was buried west of Ye and posthumously given the title Emperor Gong'ai of Chu, to console the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year he was buried west of Ye and posthumously given the title Emperor Gong'ai of Chu, to console the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 有遺腹四男，生數月，皆幽死。

translations.literal: There were four posthumous sons; within a few months of birth, all were secretly killed.
translations.idiomatic: There were four posthumous sons; within a few months of birth, all were secretly killed.

sentences.zh: 以平陽王淹孫世俊嗣。

translations.literal: Prince Yan of Pingyang's grandson Shijun was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan of Pingyang's grandson Shijun was made heir.

sentences.zh: 儼妃李祖欽女也，進為楚帝后，居宣則宮，齊亡，乃嫁焉。

translations.literal: Yan's consort was a daughter of Li Zuqin; she was promoted to Empress of the Emperor of Chu and resided in Xuanze Palace. When Qi fell, she remarried.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's consort was a daughter of Li Zuqin. She was promoted to Empress of the Emperor of Chu and resided in Xuanze Palace. When Qi fell, she remarried.

sentences.zh: 齊安王廓，字仁弘，武成第四子也。

translations.literal: Prince Kuo of Qi'an, style Renhong, was Wucheng's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kuo of Qi'an, style Renhong, was the fourth son of Emperor Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 性長者，無過行，位特進、開府儀同三司、定州刺史。

translations.literal: By nature he was a man of forbearance, without misconduct; he held the posts of Special Advancement, Opener of a Government Office with Equivalence to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was a man of forbearance and without misconduct. He held the posts of Special Advancement, Opener of a Government Office with Equivalence to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 北平王貞，字仁堅，武成第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Zhen of Beiping, style Renjian, was Wucheng's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhen of Beiping, style Renjian, was the fifth son of Emperor Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 沉審寬恕，帝常曰：「此兒得我鳳毛。

translations.literal: Deep, careful, and forgiving, the emperor often said, "This boy has inherited my fine plumage.
translations.idiomatic: Deep, careful, and forgiving, the emperor often said, "This boy has inherited my fine plumage.

sentences.zh: 」位司州牧、京畿大都督、兼尚書令、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Governor of Sizhou, Grand Commander of the Capital Region, concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Recorder of Affairs in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Governor of Sizhou, Grand Commander of the Capital Region, concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Recorder of Affairs in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝行幸，總留台事。

translations.literal: When the emperor traveled, Zhen took overall charge of affairs at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, Zhen took overall charge of affairs at the capital.

sentences.zh: 積年，後主以貞長大，漸忌之。

translations.literal: Over the years, as Zhen grew to maturity, the Last Ruler gradually came to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years, as Zhen grew to maturity, the Last Ruler gradually came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 阿那肱承旨，令馮士幹劾，系貞於獄，奪其留後權。

translations.literal: An Nagu, following the emperor's intent, had Feng Shigan impeach him, imprisoned Zhen, and stripped him of his authority as regent at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An Nagu, following the emperor's intent, had Feng Shigan impeach him, imprisoned Zhen, and stripped him of his authority as regent at the capital.

sentences.zh: 高平王仁英，武成第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince Renying of Gaoping was Wucheng's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Renying of Gaoping was the sixth son of Emperor Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 舉止軒昂，精神無檢格。

translations.literal: His bearing was lofty, and his spirit was unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was lofty, and his spirit was unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 位定州刺史。

translations.literal: He held the post of Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮南王仁光，武成第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince Renguang of Huainan was Wucheng's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Renguang of Huainan was the seventh son of Emperor Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 性躁又暴，位清都尹。

translations.literal: By nature he was irritable and violent; he held the post of Prefect of Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was irritable and violent. He held the post of Prefect of Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 次西河王仁機，生而無骨，不自支持。

translations.literal: Next was Prince Renji of Xihe, born without firm bones and unable to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Prince Renji of Xihe, born without firm bones and unable to support himself.

sentences.zh: 次樂平王仁邕；

translations.literal: Next was Prince Renyong of Leping;
translations.idiomatic: Next was Prince Renyong of Leping;

sentences.zh: 次潁川王仁儉；

translations.literal: next was Prince Renjian of Yingchuan;
translations.idiomatic: next was Prince Renjian of Yingchuan;

sentences.zh: 次安樂王仁雅，從小有暗疾；

translations.literal: next was Prince Renya of Anle, who from childhood had a speech ailment;
translations.idiomatic: next was Prince Renya of Anle, who from childhood had a speech ailment;

sentences.zh: 次丹楊王仁直；

translations.literal: next was Prince Renzhi of Danyang;
translations.idiomatic: next was Prince Renzhi of Danyang;

sentences.zh: 次東海王仁謙，皆養于北宮。

translations.literal: and next was Prince Renqian of Donghai—all were raised in the Northern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: and next was Prince Renqian of Donghai—all were raised in the Northern Palace.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王死後，諸王守禁彌切。

translations.literal: After Prince Yan of Langye died, the restrictions on the princes grew ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Yan of Langye died, the restrictions on the princes grew ever tighter.

sentences.zh: 武平末年，仁邕已下，始得出外，供給儉薄，取充而已。

translations.literal: In the last years of Wuping, Renyong and those below him were at last allowed to go outside; their supplies were meager, barely enough to get by.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Wuping, Renyong and those below him were at last allowed to go outside. Their supplies were meager, barely enough to get by.

sentences.zh: 尋後主窮蹙，以廓為光州，貞為青州，仁英為冀州，仁儉為膠州，仁直為濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon, as the Last Ruler fell into desperate straits, Kuo was sent to Guangzhou, Zhen to Qingzhou, Renying to Jizhou, Renjian to Jiaozhou, and Renzhi to serve as Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, as the Last Ruler fell into desperate straits, Kuo was sent to Guangzhou, Zhen to Qingzhou, Renying to Jizhou, Renjian to Jiaozhou, and Renzhi to serve as Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 自廓已下，多與後主死于長安。

translations.literal: From Kuo downward, most died together with the Last Ruler in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: From Kuo downward, most died together with the Last Ruler in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 仁英以清狂，仁雅以喑疾，獲免，俱徙蜀。

translations.literal: Renying, because of his wild eccentricity, and Renya, because of his speech ailment, were spared and both were transferred to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Renying, because of his wild eccentricity, and Renya, because of his speech ailment, were spared and both were transferred to Shu.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，追仁英，詔與蕭琮、陳叔寶修其本宗祭祀。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, Renying was recalled and ordered, together with Xiao Cong and Chen Shubao, to maintain the sacrifices of his original clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, Renying was recalled and ordered, together with Xiao Cong and Chen Shubao, to maintain the sacrifices of his original clan.

sentences.zh: 未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 後主五男：穆皇后生幼主；

translations.literal: The Last Ruler had five sons: Empress Mu bore the Infant Ruler;
translations.idiomatic: The Last Ruler had five sons: Empress Mu bore the Infant Ruler;

sentences.zh: 諸姬生東平王恪，次善德，次質德，次質錢；

translations.literal: consorts bore Prince Ke of Dongping, then Shande, then Zhide, then Zhiqian;
translations.idiomatic: consorts bore Prince Ke of Dongping, then Shande, then Zhide, then Zhiqian;

sentences.zh: 胡太后以恪嗣琅邪王，尋夭折。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu made Ke heir to Prince Yan of Langye, but he soon died young.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu made Ke heir to Prince Yan of Langye, but he soon died young.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，周武帝以任城已下大小三十王歸長安，皆有封爵。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou sent the thirty princes great and small from Prince Rencheng downward back to Chang'an, all receiving titles of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou sent the thirty princes great and small from Prince Rencheng downward back to Chang'an, all receiving titles of nobility.

sentences.zh: 其後不從戮者，散配西土，皆死邊。

translations.literal: Afterward those who were not executed with the rest were scattered and assigned to the western regions, and all died on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward those who were not executed with the rest were scattered and assigned to the western regions, and all died on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 論曰：文襄諸子，咸有風骨。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The sons of Prince Wenxiang all possessed force of character.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The sons of Prince Wenxiang all possessed force of character.

sentences.zh: 雖文雅之道，有謝間、平，然武藝英姿，多堪禦侮。

translations.literal: Although in the way of literary refinement they fell short of Jian and Ping, in martial skill and heroic bearing many were fit to repel insult.
translations.idiomatic: Although in literary refinement they fell short of the likes of Lin Xiangru and Lord Pingyuan, in martial skill and heroic bearing many were fit to repel insult.

sentences.zh: 縱咸陽賜劍，殲覆有徵，若使蘭陵獲全，未可量也。

translations.literal: Even if swords had been granted at Xianyang and signs of annihilation had appeared, had Prince Changgong of Lanling been preserved whole, the outcome could not have been measured.
translations.idiomatic: Even if swords had been granted at Xianyang and signs of annihilation had already appeared, had Prince Changgong of Lanling been preserved, the outcome might have been beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 而終見誅翦，以至土崩，可為太息者矣。

translations.literal: Yet in the end they were executed and cut down, until the state collapsed—a matter for deep sighing indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end they were executed and cut down until the state collapsed—a matter for deep sighing indeed.

sentences.zh: 安德以時艱主暗，晦跡韜光；

translations.literal: Prince Ande, because the times were hard and the ruler benighted, hid his tracks and concealed his brilliance;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ande, because the times were hard and the ruler benighted, hid his tracks and concealed his brilliance;

sentences.zh: 及平陽之陣，奮其忠勇，蓋以臨難見危，義深家國。

translations.literal: at the battle of Pingyang he exerted his loyalty and courage—surely because, facing danger in crisis, his devotion to state and family ran deep.
translations.idiomatic: at the battle of Pingyang he exerted his loyalty and courage—surely because, facing danger in crisis, his devotion to state and family ran deep.

sentences.zh: 德昌大舉，事迫群情，理至淪亡，無所歸命。

translations.literal: Dechang's great campaign was forced by popular feeling; reason led all the way to ruin, and there was nowhere to turn for deliverance.
translations.idiomatic: The Dechang campaign was forced by popular feeling; reason led all the way to ruin, and there was nowhere to turn for deliverance.

sentences.zh: 廣甯請出後宮，竟不獲遂，非孝珩辭致，有謝李同，自是後主心識，去平原已遠。

translations.literal: Guangning's request to lead troops out of the rear palace was ultimately not granted; it was not that Xiaohang lacked eloquence, but that he fell short of Li Tong. From then on the Last Ruler's understanding was far removed from Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaohang of Guangning's request to lead troops out of the rear palace was ultimately not granted. It was not that Xiaohang lacked eloquence, but that he fell short of Li Tong. From then on the Last Ruler's understanding was far removed from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 存亡事異，安可同年而說。

translations.literal: Survival and destruction are different matters—how can they be spoken of in the same breath?
translations.idiomatic: Survival and destruction are different matters—how can they be spoken of in the same breath?

sentences.zh: 武成殘忍奸穢，事極人倫；

translations.literal: Wucheng was cruel, wicked, and debauched, his conduct exceeding the bounds of human relations;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng was cruel, wicked, and debauched, his conduct exceeding the bounds of human relations;

sentences.zh: 太原跡異猜嫌，情非釁逆，禍起昭信，遂及淫刑。

translations.literal: Prince Shaode of Taiyuan's conduct aroused suspicion, yet his intent was not rebellion; disaster arose from Zhaoxin, and excessive punishments followed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaode of Taiyuan's conduct aroused suspicion, yet his intent was not rebellion. Disaster arose from Zhaoxin, and excessive punishments followed.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 欲求長世，未之有也。

translations.literal: To seek long life for the dynasty—there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: To seek long life for the dynasty—there has never been such a thing.

sentences.zh: 以孝昭德音，庶可慶流後嗣，百年之酷，蓋濟南之濫觴。

translations.literal: With Xiaozhao's virtuous pronouncement, blessings might have flowed to later generations; a century of cruelty had its source in the Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: With Emperor Xiaozhao's virtuous pronouncement, blessings might have flowed to later generations. A century of cruelty had its source in the Prince of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 其云「莫效前人」之言，可為傷歎。

translations.literal: His words, "Do not imitate your predecessors," are a matter for grief and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: His words, "Do not imitate your predecessors," are a matter for grief and sighing.

sentences.zh: 各愛其子，豈其然乎？

translations.literal: Each loving his own son—is it really so?
translations.idiomatic: Each loving his own son—is it really so?

sentences.zh: 琅邪雖無師傅之資，而早聞氣尚，士開淫亂，多曆歲年，一朝剿絕，慶集朝野，以之受斃，深可痛焉。

translations.literal: Although Prince Yan of Langye lacked the training of tutors, he early showed force of character. He Shikai's debauchery had lasted many years; in one morning it was cut off, and rejoicing filled court and countryside. That he was put to death for it is deeply lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Although Prince Yan of Langye lacked the training of tutors, he early showed force of character. He Shikai's debauchery had lasted many years; in one morning it was cut off, and rejoicing filled court and countryside. That he was put to death for it is deeply lamentable.

sentences.zh: 然專戮之釁，未之或免。

translations.literal: Yet the offense of unauthorized execution could scarcely be escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the offense of unauthorized execution could scarcely be escaped.

sentences.zh: 贈帝諡恭，矯枉過直。

translations.literal: To posthumously grant him an emperor's title and the posthumous name Gong was to overcorrect past wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: To posthumously grant him an emperor's title and the posthumous name Gong was to overcorrect past wrongs.

sentences.zh: 觀過知仁，不亦異於是乎！

translations.literal: To know virtue by observing faults—is it not different from this!
translations.idiomatic: To know virtue by observing faults—is it not different from this!
